eng:
1. 	The Work of the Spirit 	Sun, Aug 9
a. 	What lesson did Christ teach in describing the work of conversion? John 3:5–8.
“A person may not be able to tell the exact time or place, or trace all the chain of circumstances in the process of conversion; but this does not prove him to be unconverted. .  .  .  Like the wind, which is invisible, yet the effects of which are plainly seen and felt, is the Spirit of God in its work upon the human heart. That regenerating power, which no human eye can see, begets a new life in the soul; it creates a new being in the image of God.”—Steps to Christ, p. 57.
b. 	What changes will appear in the life of the truly converted? Romans 12:9–18; 2 Corinthians 5:17.
“While we cannot do anything to change our hearts or to bring ourselves into harmony with God; while we must not trust at all to ourselves or our good works, our lives will reveal whether the grace of God is dwelling within us. A change will be seen in the character, the habits, the pursuits. The contrast will be clear and decided between what they have been and what they are. . . .
“It is true that there may be an outward correctness of deportment without the renewing power of Christ. The love of influence and the desire for the esteem of others may produce a well-ordered life. Self-respect may lead us to avoid the appearance of evil. A selfish heart may perform generous actions. By what means, then, shall we determine whose side we are on?
“Who has the heart? With whom are our thoughts?”—Ibid., pp. 57, 58.
bem:
1.   UMULIMO WA MUPASHI                                                                                           Cimo, Aug 9
a. 	Lisambililo nshi lintu Yesu akwete ukufundisha mukwesha ukulondolola umulimo wakwalulwa? Yohane 3:5–8.
“Umuntu tengakwanisha ukulondolola inshita atemwa  incende kabili teti abe uwa kukutuluka imbela iya mu mutande wakwalulwa ; lelo ici tacikwata ukulangisha ukuti ena taba uwa kupilibuka. .  .  . Ngomwela uyo uushikwata ukumoneka, lelo icipupu ca uko cena cilakwata ukumonwa kabili nokumfwika  mukumwensekesha, efibomba umupashi wakwa Lesa pa mutima wa muntu. yalya amaka ayakubumbulula , ayo umuntu nangu umo tengakwanisha ukumona namenso ya bu muntu, eyaleta imupashi upya mu mweo; aya amaka yakwata ukuleta ububtu ubupya mu cipasho cakwa Lesa  .”—Steps to Christ, p. 57.
b. 	Kwalulwa nshi uku kakwata ukumoneka mu mweo wa uyo uwakwata ukulapila mu cishinka? Abena Roma 12:9–18; 2 Kolinto5:17.
“Nangula cingaba cakuti tekuti tucite icili conse mukwalula imitima Yesu atemwa ukuipalamika fwebene fweka mubwampano na Lesa wesu;  Nangula cakutila tekutti tube abakuicetekela fwebene fweka mumbelafye iili yonse atemwa imilimo Yesu ine iisuma, imyeo Yesu ilinokuba iyakusokolola nga cakutila icikuku cakwa Lesa cili icakwikala muli ifwe atemwa iyo. Ukwalulwa kuli no kumoneka mu mubele, mu myata pamofye na muficitwa. no bupusano buli no kumwensekesha no kupampamikwa pakati kapafyo bakwete ukuba elyo napafyo bali nomba . . .
“Cacine icakuti kuti kwabako ukulungamikwa ukwa kunse  ukwa kuipelesha lelo ukwabula amaka ayakwa Klistu  ayakubumbulula. Ukutemwa kwa lwambu pamofye no bukabilo ubwa kusansabikwa [uksumbulwa] abantu bambi kuti kwaba ukwa kuleta umweo uwaba munkonka.  ukuicindamika kuti kwaba ukwa kututungulwilafye muku fulumuka kwa kumoneka kwa bubifi. umutima wabukaitemwe kuti wakwata ukubomba ne milimo iya nkumbu. Eico nomba kanshi ni mushila nshi tuli no kwishibilako ulubali luntu twaba abakusangwako?
“Nani uuli no mutima ? Kabili nipali ani apali amalangulushi yesu?”—Ibid.,pp. 57, 58

eng:
2. 	To Be A New Creature 	Mon, Aug 10
a. 	What fruit is produced by those filled with the Spirit? Galatians 5:22, 23.
“Those who become new creatures in Christ Jesus will bring forth the fruits of the Spirit. . . . The things they once hated they now love, and the things they once loved they hate. The proud and self-assertive become meek and lowly in heart. The vain and supercilious become serious and unobtrusive. The drunken become sober, and the profligate pure. The vain customs and fashions of the world are laid aside. Christians will seek not the ‘outward adorning,’ but ‘the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit.’ 1 Peter 3:3, 4.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 58, 59.
“The influence of the Holy Spirit is the life of Christ in the soul. We do not see Christ and speak to Him, but His Holy Spirit is just as near us in one place as in another. It works in and through every one who receives Christ. Those who know the indwelling of the Spirit reveal the fruits of the Spirit—love, joy, peace, long-suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 6, p. 1112.
b. 	What is the evidence of genuine repentance? Ezekiel 33:14, 15.
“There is no evidence of genuine repentance unless it works reformation. If he restore the pledge, give again that he had robbed, confess his sins, and love God and his fellowmen, the sinner may be sure that he has passed from death unto life.
“When, as erring, sinful beings, we come to Christ and become partakers of His pardoning grace, love springs up in the heart. Every burden is light, for the yoke that Christ imposes is easy. Duty becomes a delight, and sacrifice a pleasure. The path that before seemed shrouded in darkness, becomes bright with beams from the Sun of Righteousness.
“The loveliness of the character of Christ will be seen in His followers. It was His delight to do the will of God. Love to God, zeal for His glory, was the controlling power in our Saviour’s life. Love beautified and ennobled all His actions. Love is of God. The unconsecrated heart cannot originate or produce it. It is found only in the heart where Jesus reigns. ‘We love, because He first loved us.’ 1 John 4:19, R.V. In the heart renewed by divine grace, love is the principle of action. It modifies the character, governs the impulses, controls the passions, subdues enmity, and ennobles the affections. This love, cherished in the soul, sweetens the life and sheds a refining influence on all around.”—Steps to Christ, p. 59.
bem:
2.  UKUBA ICILENGWA CIPYA                                                                             Cibili, Aug 10
a. 	Cisabo nshi icikwata Ukufuma mui abo abesushiwamo no mupashi? Abena Galatia 5:22, 23.
“Abo bonse abakwata ukwalulwa ifilengwa fipya muli Yesu Klistu  bali no kulangisha ifisabo fya bumupashi. . . . ne fintu bakwete ukupata pakashita kamo apa nomba baba abakufitemwa kabili ne fintu ifyo bakwete ukutemwa apa nomba bakwata ukufipata. Abali ne cilumba pamofye no kuisubila apa nomba bayaluka abaicefya kabili abainasha mu mitima yabo. Kabili abali abamiya pamofye nabaleisansabika apa nomba baba abayolompa na kabili abacilela [abansansa]. Abakolelwe bayaluka abaicefya kabili abakoweshiwe bayaluka abasanguluka. Nentambi ishabula ubuyo nefya cise-ise ifya mucalo fyabikwa pambali. Abena Klistu tabakakabile ukuyemba kwa kunse nakalya iyo lelo bakalafwaya bu muntu ubwa fiswa ubwa mu mutima ubo ubushibonsa pamofye noku cindamikwa ukwa bafuka kabili ababa no mupashi uwatekanya.  ’ 1 Petelo 3:3, 4.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 58, 59.
“Ulwambu ulwa mupashi wa mushilo lwaba e mweo wakwa Klistu  mu mupashi. tatukwata ukumona Klistu  nokuba abakulanshanya nankwe , lelo umupashi wakwe wakwata ukubafye mupepi-pepi mucifulo cimo kabili necibiye. Uukwata ukubombela muli uyo onse uukwata ukupokelela Klistu . abo bonse abakwata ukwiluka ukwikala kwa mupashi balakwata ukuba abakusokolola ifisabo fya bumupashi. ifyaba kutemwa, insansa, ubupete, ubusuma, pamofye ne citetekelo.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 6, p. 1112.
b. 	Cishininkisho nshi icakulapila ukwa cine? Ezekele 33:14, 15.
“Takwingaba icishininkisho cakulapila ukwa cine kanofye uko ukulapila kwa leta ukufukulula. Umubembu nga cakutila akwata ukubweseshamo umulapo, no kuba uwa kupela cilya cintu akwete ukwiba palwalala [ukufinsha], atumbula ne membu shakwe no kuba uwakutemwa Lesa pamo na bantu, umubembu kuti aba uwa cetekela ukuti naba uwakupita Ukufuma kumfwa no kuya ku mweo.
“Nga bantu abamipuso, kabili ababembu, twakwata ukwisa kuli Yesu  no kwisa ba abasenda ulubali mu cikuku cakwe icakwelela; ukutemwa kulakwata ukubalika mu kati ka mutima. Ne cisendo conse cilesa mukuba icayanguka pa mulandu wakuti ikoli lintu Yesu esa mukupela lilaba ilya yanguka. Umulimo wisa mukwaluka ninsansa kabili na bulilambo nge cakusekelelamo. Ne nshila iyo kale yalemoneka iyafimbwa mumfifi ilesa mukuba iya kubutushiwa no lwengelele Ukufuma ku kasuba.
“Nokutemwa kwa mubele wakwa Klistu  kukaba ukwakumoneka muli bakakonka bakwe. Kwali kusekelela kwakwe ukucita ubufwayo bwakwa Lesa. Ukutemwa kwa kuli Lesa, ukupimpa kwa kubukata bwakwe, fyali e maka ayelekwata ukutungulula mu mweo wakwa kapususha wesu. ukutemwa e kwawemye no cindamika ificitwa fyakwe fyonse. Lesa kutemwa, eico umutima uusha shila tekuti ube uwa ku kuleta atemwa uku kulangisha. Kukwata ukusangwa mu mutima muntu Yesu abafye uwa kuteka. Twaliba abakutemwa pa mulandu wakuti Lesa e wabalilepo ukututemwa.’ 1 Yohane 4:19, R.V. Mukati ka mutima uyo uwalengwa cipya cipya ukupitila mucikuku ca buLesa, ukutemwa kwaba nge cipope ica mu cicitwa. Kulenga cipya cipya umubele, kutungulula imyumfwile pamofye nensuna, kubumbulula ubulwani no kukwata ukuwamisha imifwaile. Uku e kutemwa ukusekelelwa mukati ka mutima, kuwamisha umweo no kukwata ukulangisha ulwambu ulwakulopolola kulyabo bonse abashingulwike.”—Steps to Christ, p. 59

eng:
3. 	Two Errors 	Tue, Aug 11
a. 	What dangerous errors are accepted by many professed Christians? Philippians 3:9; Romans 10:3; James 2:17.
“There are two errors against which the children of God—particularly those who have just come to trust in His grace—especially need to guard. The first, already dwelt upon, is that of looking to their own works, trusting to anything they can do, to bring themselves into harmony with God. He who is trying to become holy by his own works in keeping the law, is attempting an impossibility. All that man can do without Christ is polluted with selfishness and sin. It is the grace of Christ alone, through faith, that can make us holy.
“The opposite and no less dangerous error is that belief in Christ releases men from keeping the law of God; that since by faith alone we become partakers of the grace of Christ, our works have nothing to do with our redemption.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 59, 60.
b. 	How does the new covenant promise make it evident that the grace of Christ does not exempt us from obedience to God’s law? Hebrews 8:10; 10:16.
“The law of God is an expression of His very nature; it is an embodiment of the great principle of love, and hence is the foundation of His government in heaven and earth. If our hearts are renewed in the likeness of God, if the divine love is implanted in the soul, will not the law of God be carried out in the life? When the principle of love is implanted in the heart, when man is renewed after the image of Him that created him, the new-covenant promise is fulfilled [Hebrews 10:16 quoted]. And if the law is written in the heart, will it not shape the life? Obedience—the service and allegiance of love—is the true sign of discipleship.”—Ibid., p. 60.
“God requires at this time just what He required of the holy pair in Eden, perfect obedience to His requirements. His law remains the same in all ages. The great standard of righteousness presented in the Old Testament is not lowered in the New. It is not the work of the gospel to weaken the claims of God’s holy law, but to bring men up where they can keep its precepts.
“The faith in Christ which saves the soul is not what it is represented to be by many. ‘Believe, believe,’ is their cry; ‘only believe in Christ, and you will be saved. It is all you have to do.’ While true faith trusts wholly in Christ for salvation, it will lead to perfect conformity to the law of God.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 6, p. 1073.
bem:
3. 	IMIPUSO IBILI                                                                                       Citatu, Aug 11
a. 	Mipuso nshi iyabusanso iyakwata ukusuminishiwa na bengi abakwata ukuitunga ukuba abena Klistu ? Abena Filipi 3:9; Abena Roma 10:3; Yakobo 2:17.
“Kwaliba imipuso ibili intu abana bwakwa Lesa— maka-maka abo abesafye mukusumina mu cikuku cakwe— intu balingile ukuba abakuilamako. Uwakubalilapo, uyo untu waba uwakwikalilwapo kale kale, ni uyu uwakukwata ukulolesha pa milimo yabo abene, ukukwata ukusuminisha fye conse ico benga kwata ukucita, kukuileta abene beka mubwampano na Lesa. Uyo onse uulekwata ukwesha ukuba uwa mushilo ukupitila mu milimo yakwe umwine ku kukwata ukusunga ifunde, alekwata ukwesha icishingacitwa. Conse fye cintu umuntu engacita ukwabula Klistu , calikantanishiwa na bukaitemwe pamofye no lubembu. Cikuku fye cakwa Klistu epela, ukupitila mucitetekelo, e cingatulenga fye ifwe ukuba abamushilo.
“Icilubo cimbi kulubali lumbi icishili cakwangusha nici icakuti;  ukusumina muli Klistu  kulalomotola (ukufumya) abantu mukusunga ifunde lyakwa Lesa; no kutila kanshi nomba pa mulandu wakuti, ukupitila mu citetekelo ceka, tulaba abakusendamo ulubali mu cikuku cakwa Klistu, ninshi imilimo yesu fye yena tayakwata incito nangu imo ku kulubulwa kwesu.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 59, 60
b. 	Nishani ubulayo bwa cipangano cipya bwakwata ukucilenga ukumfwikishiwa icakuti icikuku cakwa Klistu tacatupatulako ifwe ku kukwata icumfwila kwi funde lyakwa Lesa? Abahebele 8:10; 10:16
“Ifunde lyakwa Lesa lyaba emubele wa mbela yakwe; caba e mwisulo onse uwa cipope icikalamba icaba icakutemwa kabili, pa muku umo wine lyaba emufula wabutungulushi bwakwe kumulu na pesonde. Nga cakutila imitima yesu yaba iya kulengwa cipya-cipya kukupalana na Lesa, nga cakutila ukutemwa kwa buLesa kwa kwata ukulimbwa mukati ka mupashi, bushe ifunde lyakwa Lesa tekuti libe ilya kubomfeshiwa mukati ka mweo? Ilyo lintu icipope cakutemwa cakwata ukulimbwa mukati ka mutima, lintu umuntu akwata ukulengwa cipya-cipya mukupalana na uyo uwa mubumbile, ubulayo bwa cipangano cipya bulakwata ukufikilishiwa [Abahebele 10:16 ngeipelwe.] Kabili nga cakuti ifunde lyakwata ukulimbwa mu mutima bushe tekuti lyalule umweo? Icumfwila icaba kubomba pamo ne cumfwila cakutemwa ifyaba nge cishibilo ca busambi ubwa cine.”—Ibid., p. 60.
“Lesa pali ino inshita alekabila fimo fine fintu akwete ukukabila kuli balya babili abali abamushilo mu Eden, icumfwila icapwililika ku mabukabilo yakwe. Ifunde lyakwe ukubelelela fye cimo cine munkulo fye shonse. Umushinku uu kalamba uwa bulungami uwalangishiwe mu cipangano cakale tawakwata ukutotobeshiwa mu cipangano cipya. Tawaba mulimo wambila nsuma ukunasha ifikabila ifunde lyakkwa Lesa ilyaba ilya mushilo, lelo ikwata ukutumpula abantu ukubaleta pantu bengakwatila ukulisunga.
“Icitetekelo muli Klistu  icikwata ukupususha umupashi tacikwata ukupelwa kubantu  abengi. Sumineni, sumineni e kubilikisha kwabo, ukusuminafye muli Yesu epela kabili walakwata ukupusushiwa. Ici cekafye eco ulingilefye ukucita. Nangula cakuti icitetekelo icacine cikwata ukusumina umupwilapo muli Klistu pakukwata ukupusushiwa, cili no kukutungulula kukucita kwefunde lyakwa Lesa ukwa mupwilapo.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 6, p. 1073.

eng:
4. 	Salvation a Free Gift 	Wed, Aug 12
a. 	What is expected of candidates for eternal life? 1 John 5:2, 3; 1 Corinthians 7:19.
“If you give yourself to [Christ], and accept Him as your Saviour, then, sinful as your life may have been, for His sake you are accounted righteous. Christ’s character stands in place of your character, and you are accepted before God just as if you had not sinned.
“More than this, Christ changes the heart. He abides in your heart by faith. You are to maintain this connection with Christ by faith and the continual surrender of your will to Him; and so long as you do this, He will work in you to will and to do according to His good pleasure. So you may say, ‘The life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave Himself for me.’ Galatians 2:20. So Jesus said to His disciples, ‘It is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.’ Matthew 10:20. Then with Christ working in you, you will manifest the same spirit and do the same good works—works of righteousness, obedience.
“So we have nothing in ourselves of which to boast. We have no ground for self-exaltation. Our only ground of hope is in the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and in that wrought by His Spirit working in and through us.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 62, 63.
b. 	Although the Lord has made provision for all to obtain salvation, why do some miss the way? Ephesians 2:8, 9; Acts 4:12; Romans 9:30–33.
“Instead of releasing man from obedience, it is faith, and faith only, that makes us partakers of the grace of Christ, which enables us to render obedience. . . .
“That so-called faith in Christ which professes to release men from the obligation of obedience to God, is not faith, but presumption. ‘By grace are ye saved through faith.’ But ‘faith, if it hath not works, is dead.’ Ephesians 2:8; James 2:17. Jesus said of Himself before He came to earth, ‘I delight to do Thy will, O My God: yea, Thy law is within My heart.’ Psalm 40:8. And just before He ascended again to heaven He declared, ‘I have kept My Father’s commandments, and abide in His love.’ John 15:10. The Scripture says, ‘Hereby we do know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. . . . He that saith he abideth in Him ought himself also so to walk even as He walked.’ 1 John 2:3–6. ‘Because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow His steps.’ 1 Peter 2:21.”—Ibid., pp. 60–62.
bem:
4.  IPUSUKILO ICABUPE ICALUTU                                                                             Cine, Aug 12
a. Cinshi cilekwata ukukabilwa ku bantu abali abalinga ukukwata umweo wa muyayaya? 1 Yohane 5:2, 3; 1 Kolinto7:19.
“Ngawakwata ukuipela we mwine kuli Klistu , no kuba uwa ku mupokelela nga kapususha obe, ilyo linefye, nangula wingaba umubembu wa musango shani kunshita ya kunuma, pamulandu fye wakwe uli uwaitwa umulungami. Umubele wakwa Klistu  ulaba uwakwiminina mu cifulo camubele obe,  kabili uli uwapokelelwa kuntanshi yakwa Lesa kwati fye nalimo twawatalile aubembukanapo.
“Ukucilapo na pali ici, Klistu  alakwata ukwalula umutima. Alakwata no kwikala mu mutima obe ukupitila mucitetekelo. Eico ulingile ukusungilila ubu ubwampano na Klistu  ukupitila mu citetekelo kabili pamofye no kutwalilila ukutula ukwa bufwayo bobe kuli wena;  Eico cikulufye wakwata ukucita ici ali no kubomba muli iwe kuli kampingu kabili na kukubomba ukulingana no bufwayo bwakwe ubusuma. Epakutila, ube uwakusosa auti, umweo untu nkwete nomba muli bumubili, ndeikala ukupitila mu citetekelo mu mwana wakwa Lesa kabili akwete ukuipela umwine eka pali ine.’ Galatia 2:20. Eico Yesu asosele ku basambi bakwe ati,‘Te iwe uulesosa nomba, lelo mupashi wakwa tata eulekwata ukulandila muli iwe..’ Mateo 10:20. Eico kanshi na Klistu uu lebomba muli iwe, ali no kulangisha umupashi umo wine no kuba uwakubomba imilimo imo ine iisuma—imilimo iya bulungami pamofye ne cumfwila.
“Kanshi tatwakwata icili conse muli fwebene ico cintu twingaitakishishamo. Tatukwetepo icifulo icaku isansabika fwebene. I ncende imo fye mpo iyesubilo yaba mu bulungami bwakwa Klistu ubo ubwakwata ukubikwa pali baifwe, kabili ni muli ico e mwakwata ukuletelwa ukubomba kwa mupashi wakwe muli baifwe..”—Steps to Christ, pp. 62, 63.
Nangula cakutila Lesa alikwata ukuleta ishuko ukuti bonse bengakwata ukusanga ipusukilo, mulandu nshi bambi bakwatila ukupusa inshila? Abena Efeso 2:8, 9; Imilimo ya batumwa 4:12; Abena Roma 9:30–33.
“Mucifulo cakulomotola umuntu Ukufuma ku cumfwila, cabafye citetekelo kabili icitetekelo fye ceka , icingalenga ifwe ukusendamo ulubali mu cikuku cakwa Klistu  ico icitulenga ifwe ukukwata icumfwila.
“Icicine icitwa ati icitetekelo muli Klistu  ico cine icikwata ukutungwa ukuba icakulomotola (ukulubula) abantu ukubafumya kukushingamwa kwa kukwata icumfwila kuli Lesa; ala ico tecitetekelo lelo kutakalala. Mu cikuku twalikwata ukupusushiwa ukupitila mucitetekelo. Lelo icitetekelo, nga cakutila tacikwete imilimo, ninshi cintu cafwa.’ Abena Efeso 2:8; Yakobo 2:17. Yesu asosele ici pa cikumine umwine, lintu ali talaisa pesonde; insekelela ukucita ubufwayo bobe, we Lesa wandi, mucinefye ifunde lyobe lyaikala mu mutima wandi.’ Amalumbo 40:8. Kabili mupepi-pepi fye no kululwa kwakwe ukuya kumulu, asosele ati, ninsunga amafunde yakwa tata no kwikalila mukutemwa kwakwe.’ Yohane 15:10. Icalembwa cisosa aciti, ni muli ici emo twishibila ukuti twalimwishiba, ngatwasunga amafunde yakwe. . . .Uyo onse uutila naikala muli wena afwile ukwenda filya ena aendele’ 1 Yohane 2:3–6. ‘Pa mulandu wakuti, Klistu  akwete ukucula pa mulandu wesu, ukutushila ifwe icilangililo icakuti, tufwile ukukonka intampulo shakwe 1 Petelo 2:21.”—Ibid., pp. 60–62

eng:
5. 	Abiding by Faith 	Thu, Aug 13
a. 	How did the apostle Paul live victoriously? 1 Corinthians 15:30, 31.
“You are to maintain this connection with Christ by faith and the continual surrender of your will to Him; and so long as you do this; He will work in you to will and to do according to His good pleasure.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 62, 63.
“Christ in His humanity wrought out a perfect character, and this character He offers to impart to us. ‘All our righteousness are as filthy rags.’ Isaiah 64:6. Everything that we of ourselves can do is defiled by sin. But the Son of God ‘was manifested to take away our sins; and in Him is no sin.’ . . . Christ was obedient to every requirement of the law. He said of Himself, ‘I delight to do Thy will, O My God; yea, Thy law is within My heart.’ Psalm 40:8. . . . By His perfect obedience He has made it possible for every human being to obey God’s commandments. When we submit ourselves to Christ, the heart is united with His heart, the will is merged in His will, the mind becomes one with His mind, the thoughts are brought into captivity to Him; we live His life. This is what it means to be clothed with the garment of His righteousness.”—Christ’s Object Lessons, pp. 311, 312.
b. 	What joy did the psalmist express in his own life? Psalm 119:97.
“When we speak of faith, there is a distinction that should be borne in mind. There is a kind of belief that is wholly distinct from faith. The existence and power of God, the truth of His word, are facts that even Satan and his hosts cannot at heart deny. The Bible says that ‘the devils also believe, and tremble;’ but this is not faith. James 2:19. Where there is not only a belief in God’s word, but a submission of the will to Him; where the heart is yielded to Him, the affections fixed upon Him, there is faith—faith that works by love and purifies the soul. Through this faith the heart is renewed in the image of God.”—Steps to Christ, p. 63.
bem:
5. 	UKWIKALILILA MU CITETEKELO                                                              Cisano, Aug 13 a. a.  Nishani umutumwa Paulo aeseshe ukwikala umweo wa bukacimfya? 1 Kolinto15:30, 31.
“Ufwile ukusungilila ubu ubwampano na Klistu  ukupitila mu citetekelo pamofye no kutwalilila ukutula ubufwayo bobe kuli wena; kabili cikulufye waba uwakucita ici, ali no kubomba muli  iwe kubufwayo na kukubomba ukulingana no bufwayo bwakwe ubusuma  .”—Steps to Christ, pp. 62, 63.
“Klistu  muli bu muntu bwakwe, aeseshe ukuleta umubele uwafikapo, Eico uyu umubele alakwata uku upela pamofye noku ubika muli baifwe.  ‘Bonse fye ubulungami bwesu fwebene bwaba nge fitatilo.’ Esaya 64:6. Conse fye ico cintu twingakwata ukucita pa lwesu calikwata ukukoweshiwa no lubembu. lelo umwana wakwa Lesa alikwete ukumoneka, ku kusenda imembu shesu; kabili muli wena twamwaba lubembu.’ . . .  Yesu aali uwa cumfwila kuli conse icikabila ifunde. Ailandile ifi umwine, ‘nsekelela ukucita ubufwayo bobe, we Lesa wandi ; Cishinka fye ifunde lyobe lyaba mu mutima wandi. Amalumbo 40:8. . . .ukupitila mu cumfwila cakwe icafikapo, alicilenga ukuba icayanguka umuntunse onse ukuba uwa kunakila amafunde yakwa Lesa. Nga twakwata ukuinasha fwebene fweka kuli Klistu, umutima ulakwata ukwampana no mutima wakwe, ubufwayo bulakwata ukulundinkanishiwa no bufwayo bwakwe, ilangulushi lisamukuba limo ne langulushi lyakwe, amatontonkanyo yesa mukuba pesamba lya butungulushi bwakwe; tutendeka ukwikala umweo wakwe. ifi efyo cikwata ukupilibula ukufwikwa no mwingila wa bulungami.”—Christ’s Object Lessons, pp. 311, 312.
b. 	Kusekelela nshi kuntu shi malumbo aeseshe ukulangisha mu mweo wakwe? Amalumbo 119:97.
“Lintu twaba abakulanda pa cikumine icitetekelo, kufwile kwaba ukulekanya ukufwile kwamoneka mukati kelangulushi. kwalibako ubusumino bumo ubo ubwakwata ukuba ubwaibela umupwilapo Ukufuma ku citetekelo. Ukubapo pamofye na maka yakwa Lesa, icine i ceshiwi lyakwe fyaba ficitwa ifyo fintu na shetani wine pamo ne fibambe fyakwe tekuti babe abakupinkana na fyo mukati ka mitima yqbo. icipingo citila,  ifiwa nafyo fine filasumina  no kututuma;’ Lelo ici te citetekelo. Yakobo 2:19. Umo umushaba ukusumina fye epela ukwa mwishiwi lyakwa Lesa lelo no kukwata ukunakila ubufwayo bwa kuli wena,  umo umutima ukwata ukucimba kuli wena pamofye ne myumfwile iya shintilila pali wena; palya pali icitetekelo – icitetekelo ico icibomela mukutemwa pamo fye no kusangulula umweo. Ukupitila muli ici icitetekelo, umutima ulalengwa cipya-cipya mu cipasho cakwa Lesa.”—Steps to Christ, p. 63.

eng:
1. 	Keys to Growth 	Sun, Aug 16
a. 	How does Scripture illustrate Christian development? Isaiah 61:3; 1 Peter 2:2; Ephesians 4:14, 15; Mark 4:26, 27.
“Not all the wisdom and the skill of man can produce life in the smallest object in nature. It is only through the life which God Himself has imparted, that either plant or animal can live. So it is only through the life from God that spiritual life is begotten in the hearts of men.”—Steps to Christ, p. 67.
b. 	What illustrates our dependence on Christ for growth and development? Hosea 14:5–7; 1 Corinthians 3:6, 7.
“In the matchless gift of His Son, God has encircled the whole world with an atmosphere of grace as real as the air which circulates around the globe. All who choose to breathe this life-giving atmosphere will live and grow up to the stature of men and women in Christ Jesus.
“As the flower turns to the sun, that the bright beams may aid in perfecting its beauty and symmetry, so should we turn to the Sun of Righteousness, that heaven’s light may shine upon us, that our character may be developed into the likeness of Christ.”—Ibid., p. 68.
bem:
1. IMFUNGULO KU KULUNDULUKA	Cimo, Aug 16
a. 	Nishani amalembo yesha ukulondolola ukulunduka kwa bwina Klistu? Esaya 61:3; 1 Petelo 2:2; Abena Efeso 4:14, 15; Mako 4:26, 27.
“Te yonse amano atemwa ukucenjelesha kwa muntu ukwingakwata ukuleta umweo mutuntu utwacepesha utusangwa mu bubumbo. Lelo kupitilafye mu mweo untu Lesa umwine eka akwata ukupela uulenga ukuti cibe cimuti atemwa ni nama ukusuminishiwa ukuba no mweo.  Eico kanshi kupitilafye mu mweo uwakufuma kuli Lesa e mukwata ukutuntuka umweo wa bumupashi mu mitima ya bantu nse.”—Steps to Christ, p. 67.
b. 	Cinshi cilondolola ishintililo lyesu pali Klistu ukukwata ukukula pamo fye no kulunduluka? Hosea 14:5–7; 1 Kolinto3:6, 7.
“Mu cabupe icishingalondololwa icamwana wakwe, Lesa alikwata ukushingulusha  icalo fye conse no mwela wa cikuku mumbela fye imo ine ngo uyu winefye umwela uukwata ukupunga mu calo fye conse. Eico bonse abasalapo ukupemako uyu umwela bakakwata no kuba abakukula ku mushinku wa baume na banakashi muli Yesu Klistu .
“Ngefyo iluba likwata ukwalukila ku kasuba pakutila fye ukubengeshima kwa lwengelele kube ukwa kwafwilisha mu kuwaminisha ubusuma bwa liko pamofye ne mimonekele ya liko, efyo cingaba nga cakutila twakwete ukwalukila ku kasuba ka bulungami, lulya ulubuto lwa kumulu kuti lwaba ulwakubalikila pali baifwe, no kulenga imibele yesu ukuba iya kwalukila mu cipasho cakwa Klistu  .”—Ibid., p.

eng:
2. 	Our Helpless Condition 	Mon, Aug 17
a. 	What important point did our Lord emphasize to His disciples just before He finished His earthly ministry? John 15:4–7.
“Many have an idea that they must do some part of the work alone. They have trusted in Christ for the forgiveness of sin, but now they seek by their own efforts to live aright. But every such effort must fail. Jesus says, ‘Without Me ye can do nothing.’ Our growth in grace, our joy, our usefulness—all depend upon our union with Christ. It is by communion with Him, daily, hourly—by abiding in Him—that we are to grow in grace. He is not only the Author, but the Finisher of our faith. It is Christ first and last and always. He is to be with us, not only at the beginning and the end of our course, but at every step of the way.”—Steps to Christ, p. 69.
“If you are willing to learn meekness and lowliness of heart in Christ’s school, He will surely give you rest and peace. It is a terribly hard struggle to give up your own will and your own way. But this lesson learned, you will find rest and peace. Pride, selfishness, and ambition must be overcome; your will must be swallowed up in the will of Christ. The whole life may become one constant love sacrifice, every action a manifestation, and every word an utterance of love. As the life of the vine circulates through stem and cluster, descends into the lower fibers, and reaches to the topmost leaf, so will the grace and love of Christ burn and abound in the soul, sending its virtues to every part of the being, and pervading every exercise of body and mind.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 5, pp. 1091, 1092.
b. 	What is the secret of growing in Christ? Colossians 2:6; Hebrews 10:38.
“You gave yourself to God to be His wholly, to serve and obey Him, and you took Christ as your Saviour. You could not yourself atone for your sins or change your heart; but having given yourself to God, you believe that He for Christ’s sake did all this for you. By faith you became Christ’s, and by faith you are to grow up in Him—by giving and taking. You are to give all—your heart, your will, your service—give yourself to Him to obey all His requirements; and you must take all—Christ, the fullness of all blessing, to abide in your heart, to be your strength, your righteousness, your everlasting helper—to give you power to obey.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 69, 70.
bem:
2. 	UMUBELO WESU UWAPELEBELWA                                                               Cibili, Aug 1
a. 	Cikomo nshi icikankala cintu shikulu aeseshe ukukomailapo kubasambi bakwe mupepi pepi fye no kusondwelela ubutumikishi bwakwe ubwa pa calo? Yohane 15:4–7.
“Abengi balikwata ubwishibilo ubwa kuti balingile ukubombapo ulubali lumo ulwa mulimo beka. Baliba abakucetekela muli Klistu  ku kwelelwa kwa lubembu lelo nomba bakwata ukulwisha mu maka yabo abene ukuti babe abakwikala abololoke. Lelo uko ukulwisha konse kulakwata ukufilikwa. Eco Yesu asosele ati; ukwabula ine tamwingacita icintu nangu cimo.’ Ukukula kwesu mucikuku, insansa shesu, pamofye no busuma bwesu—Fyonse fikwata ukushintilila pa bwampano bwesu na Klistu, Eico kupitilafye mubwampano pamo nankwe, cila bushiku, kabili cila kashita— ukulaikalila muli wena— pakutila tube abakukula mucikuku. Tabafye nikatendeka lelo pamuku umo wine nikapwishishisha wa citetekelo cesu. cifwile cabafye ukuti Yesu eufwile ukuba intanshi, ukulekelesha kabili lyonse. Ali no kuba naifwe, tepakutendeka fye na pakulekelesha kwa mulimo wesu, lelo pali cila lutampulo ulwa bulendo bwesu.”—Steps to Christ, p. 69.
“Nga uli uwaipekanishisha ukusambilila ukuicefya no mutembo wa mutima  mwi sukulu lyakwa Klistu , mucinefye ali no kukupela ukutusha pamo fye no mutende.  Kwaliba kushashala ukwa kosesha pakuba uwakucimba ubufwayo bobe pamofye ne nshila yobe wemwine. Lelo ngawakwata ukusambilila isambililo ili ukakwata ukusanga ukutusha pamo fye no mutende. Icilumba, bukaitemwe, na cakupimpisha filingile ukucimfiwa; ubufwayo bobe bulingile bwakwata ukuseshiwapo kubufwayo bwakwa Klistu. Umweo fye onse kuti wakwata ukuba ni uyo uwakutemwa kwa bulilambo ukwa kutwalilila, kabili cila mibombele ngeya kumoneka kabili cile shiwi nge lyakulangisha ukutemwa. Ngefyo umweo wa mwangashi uu kwata ukupita mu musambo ukufikafye naku fisabo kabili no kubwesesha kulushishi lwa kwi shinte kabili no kufika kwibula lya kumpela lya musambo, efyo icikuku no kutemwa kwa kwa Klistu   fili no kwalamusha pamofye no kwikala mu mweo, ukusenda ubukumu kuli cila cilundwa ca bumuntu, kabili no kupenengula [ceceta] imibombele ya mubili pamofye ne langulushi..”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 5, pp. 1091, 1092.
b. 	Cankama nshi icaba mukulundukuka muli Klistu ?  Abena kolose 2:6; Abahebele 10:38.
“Walikwete ukuipela we mwine weka kuli Lesa uikuba uwakwe umupwilapo, ku kumutumika pamofye no kumunakila, kabili wakwete ukubula Klistu  ukuba mga kapususha obe. Ala tekuti pa lobe ube uwa kuikonsolwela imembu shobe atemwa ukwalula umutima obe; lelo pakuba uwakuipela we mwine weka kuli Lesa, ninshi wakwata ukusumina ukuti, pa mulandu wakwa Klistu, alikwete ukubomba fye ici pamulandu obe. Ukupitila mucitetekelo wayalwike uwakwa Klistu kabili ukupitila mucitetekelo uli no kukulila muli wena—ukupitila mukupela no kupokelela. Ulingile ukupela fye fyonse— Umutima obe, ubufwayo bobe, umulimo obe,— ipele we mwine umupwilapo kuli wena kuku nakila fyonse fintu akwata ukukabila; kabili ulingile ukutwalafye fyonse— Yesu, umwisulo we palo lyonse, ukwikala mu mutima obe, ukuba amaka yobe, ubulungami bobe kabili kafwa obe uwa uyayaya—pa  ku kupela iwe amaka ya kumfwila.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 69, 70.

eng:
3. 	Daily Consecration 	Tue, Aug 18
a. 	What is the first duty of God’s children as they begin each day? Psalm 5:3.
“Consecrate yourself to God in the morning; make this your very first work. Let your prayer be, ‘Take me, O Lord, as wholly Thine. I lay all my plans at Thy feet. Use me today in Thy service. Abide with me, and let all my work be wrought in Thee.’ This is a daily matter. Each morning consecrate yourself to God for that day. Surrender all your plans to Him, to be carried out or given up as His providence shall indicate. Thus day by day you may be giving your life into the hands of God, and thus your life will be molded more and more after the life of Christ.”—Steps to Christ. p. 70.
b. 	What invitation is Christ extending daily? Matthew 11:28, 29.
“A life in Christ is a life of restfulness. There may be no ecstasy of feeling, but there should be an abiding, peaceful trust. Your hope is not in yourself; it is in Christ. Your weakness is united to His strength, your ignorance to His wisdom, your frailty to His enduring might. So you are not to look to yourself, not to let the mind dwell upon self, but look to Christ. Let the mind dwell upon His love, upon the beauty, the perfection, of His character. Christ in His self-denial, Christ in His humiliation, Christ in His purity and holiness, Christ in His matchless love–this is the subject for the soul’s contemplation. It is by loving Him, copying Him, depending wholly upon Him, that you are to be transformed into His likeness.”—Ibid., pp. 70, 71.
c. 	What is the key to experiencing peace of mind? Isaiah 26:3, 4; 30:15.
“Those who take Christ at His word, and surrender their souls to His keeping, their lives to His ordering, will find peace and quietude. Nothing of the world can make them sad when Jesus makes them glad by His presence. In perfect acquiescence there is perfect rest. . . . Our lives may seem a tangle; but as we commit ourselves to the wise Master Worker, He will bring out the pattern of life and character that will be to His own glory.
“As through Jesus we enter into rest, heaven begins here. We respond to His invitation, Come, learn of Me, and in thus coming we begin the life eternal.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 331.
bem:
3. 	UKUIPELA UKWA CILA BUSHIKU                                                                   Citatu, Aug 1
a. 	Mulimo nshi uwakubalilapo uwa bana bakwa Lesa lintu balekwata ukutendeka ubushiku lyonse? Amalumbo   5:3
“Ipele we mwine kuli Lesa mulucelo; ucite ici ngo mulimo wantanshi. leka ipepo lyobe libe lyakuti, mpokeleleni Lesa wandi, ngo wenu. nabika amapange yandi pakansa shenu. Mbomfyeni ilelo ku mulimo wenu. Ikaleni naine kabili lekeni imilimo yandi yonse icitilwe mukufwaya kwenu.’ Uyu mulimo wa cilabushiku, cila lucelo ube uwakuipelesha we mwine kuli Lesa pali ubo ubushiku. Ube uwakubika amapange yobe pali wena, pakuti yabe aya bomba atemwa ukuyaleka ukulingana ngefyo ubukabilo bwakwe bwakwata ukutungulula. Eico ubushiku no bushiku uleba uwakupela umweo obe mu maboko yakwa Lesa, kabili, no mweo obe uli no kukwata ukubumbululwa kucifiko icikalamaba ku kupalana no mweo wakwa Klistu.”—Steps to Christ. p. 70.
b. 	Kulalikwa nshi kuntu Klistu alekwata ukutambalikako cilabushiku? Mateo 11:28, 29.
“Umweo muli Klistu  waba mweo umwaba ubutusho ubwafikapo. Limbi takwingaba imyumfwile yakwalamusha, lelo kulingile ukuba icitetekelo icakwikalilila kabili ica mutende. Isubilo lyobe talikwata ukusangwa muli we mwine lelo likwata ukusangwa fye muli Klistu. Ukunakuka kobe kukakwata ukuminkana ku bukose bwakwe, no kukana ishiba kobe ku mano yakwa Klistu, no bunake bobe ku bulamba bwakwe ubwa mukutwalilila. Eico taulingile ukulolesha kuli wemwine, kabili wisuminisha ilangulushi lya kushintilila pali buine, lelo ba uwa kulolesha kuli Klistu. Leka ilangulushi lyobe libe ilyakwikalilila pa kutemwa kwakwe, pa ubusuma bwakwe pamofye na pa kukupwililika kwakwe ukwa mubele. Klistu mu kuikanya kwakwe, Klistu mu kuicefya kwakwe, Klistu muli bu musangwela na bumushilo bwakwe kabili Klistu mukutemwa kwakwe ukushingalondololwa filingile fyaba e milandu iya kwetetulapo kwelangulushi. Kupitila fye mukukwata uku mutemwa ena, muku konkelesha ena, kabili na mukushintilila pali wena umupwilapo emo wingakwatila ukwalwilwa mu cipasho cakwe.”—Ibid., pp. 70, 71.
c. 	Lufungulo nshi mukuba aba kukwata icibelesho ca mutende we langulushi? Esaya 26:3, 4; 30:15.
“Abo bonse abakwata ukusenda Klistu  ukulingana nge shiwi lyakwe, no kuba aba kupela imipashi yabo umupwilapo ku busunge bwakwe, ne mweo yabo ku butungulushi bwakwe bakaba abakusanga umutende no kupepemuka. Tapengaba nangu cimo mu calo icingakwata ukubalenga ubulanda ilyo ninshi Yesu nakwata ukubalenga abansansa mukubapo kwakwe. Mukumukumanya ukwapwililika e mwaba ukutusha ukwafikapo. . . . Imyeo Yesu kuti yakwata ukumoneka iyakolobana; lelo lintu tulekwata ukuipela fwebene kuli shikulu kuli kabomba uwa mwishilo uwacilisha, akaba uwa kuleta imbela yamweo pamofye no mubele uyo uukaba wakupela ululumbi kuli wena.
“Ilyo ukupitila muli Klistu  tulekwata ukwingila mukutusha, umulu uba uwa kutendekela apapene. Tuba abakwankula ku bwite bwakwe ubwa kuti isa, sambilila kuli ine kabili pakukwata ukwisa tulakwata ukutendeka umweo wa muyayaya.”—The Desire of

eng:
4. 	Contemplation Helps Change 	Wed, Aug 19
a. 	What is the result of letting the mind dwell upon Jesus instead of looking to self? 2 Corinthians 3:18.
“By looking constantly to Jesus with the eye of faith, we shall be strengthened. God will make the most precious revelations to His hungering, thirsting people. They will find that Christ is a personal Saviour. As they feed upon His word, they find that it is spirit and life. The word destroys the natural, earthly nature, and imparts a new life in Christ Jesus. The Holy Spirit comes to the soul as a Comforter. By the transforming agency of His grace, the image of God is reproduced in the disciple; he becomes a new creature. Love takes the place of hatred, and the heart receives the divine similitude.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 391.
“When the mind dwells upon self, it is turned away from Christ, the source of strength and life. Hence it is Satan’s constant effort to keep the attention diverted from the Saviour and thus prevent the union and communion of the soul with Christ. The pleasures of the world, life’s cares and perplexities and sorrows, the faults of others, or your own faults and imperfections—to any or all of these he will seek to divert the mind. Do not be misled by his devices. Many who are really conscientious, and who desire to live for God, he too often leads to dwell upon their own faults and weaknesses, and thus by separating them from Christ he hopes to gain the victory. We should not make self the center and indulge anxiety and fear as to whether we shall be saved. All this turns the soul away from the Source of our strength. Commit the keeping of your soul to God, and trust in Him. Talk and think of Jesus. Let self be lost in Him.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 71, 72.
b. 	What can we learn from the change that came upon the disciples after they had been with Christ in daily missionary work? Acts 4:13.
“In constantly beholding [Jesus], we ‘are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.’ 2 Corinthians 3:18.
“It was thus that the early disciples gained their likeness to the dear Saviour. When those disciples heard the words of Jesus, they felt their need of Him. They sought, they found, they followed Him. They were with Him in the house, at the table, in the closet, in the field. They were with Him as pupils with a teacher, daily receiving from His lips lessons of holy truth. They looked to Him, as servants to their master, to learn their duty. Those disciples were men ‘subject to like passions as we are.’ James 5:17. They had the same battle with sin to fight. They needed the same grace, in order to live a holy life.”—Ibid., pp. 72, 73.
bem:
4. 	UKWETETULA KULAFWILISHA UKWALULWA                                           Cine, Aug 19
a. 	Cinshi cikwata Ukufuma mukusuminisha ilangulushi ukwikalilila pali Klistu  mucifulo cakulolesha kuli buine? 2 Kolinto3:18.
“Ukupitila mukutwalilila kwa kulolesha kuli Klistu  ne linso lya citetekelo, tukaba abakukoseshiwa. Lesa akakwata ukuba uwakuleta ama busokololo ayakwatisha ubukankala ku bantu bakwe bonse abo abakwete insala pamo fye ne cilaka.  Bakakwata ukusanga ukuti, Yesu ni kapususha wa cila umo. Lintu balekwata ukulya ishiwi lyakwe, besa mukusanga ukuti mupashi kabili mweo.  Ishiwi likwata ukonaula imbela ye sonde iya cifyalilwa no kuba uwakubikamo umweo upya uwa muli Klistu  Yesu. Umupashi wa mushilo wisa ku mupashi nga kakoselesha. Ukupitila mumaka ayakwalula aya cikuku cakwe, icipasho cakwa Lesa cilakwata ukulangishiwa mu musambi; Alakwata ukuba icilengwa cipya. No kutemwa kulaba ukwa kusenda icifulo ca lupato, no mutima ulakwata ukupokelela ubusuma bwa buLesa.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 391.
“Lintu ilangulushi lyakwata ukushintillila pali buine lilakwata ukufumishiwa kuli Klistu , uwaba entuntuko ya maka pamofye no mweo. Eico kanshi kwaliba kulwisha ukwa kwa shetani ukwa mukutwalilila ku kusungila kampingu ukutalushiwa Ukufuma kuli kapususha na pakapeleko ukuba uwa kucingilisha ubwampano pamo fye no kulanshanya ukwa mupashi na Klistu . Ubwangashi bwe sonde, amasakamiko yesonde, ifyakuponeka pamo fye na Malanda, ifilubo fya bantu bambi atemwa ifilubo fyobe elyo pamofye no kukana fikapo konse—Nikuli cimo pali ifi atemwa kuli fyonse fye kuntu shetani aba uwafwaisha  ukwalwila ilangulushi lyobe. Mwiba abakulufiwa nefi ifintu fyakwe. Abengi aba bumpomfu, kabili abakabila ukwikalila muli Lesa, na pali aba bene ilingiline alakwata ukwikala pa mipuso shabo elyo na mabunake yabo, kabili napakuba uwa kubapatula bene ukubafyumya kuli Klistu  alakwata ukusubila ukuba uwa kuba cimfya. Tatulingile ukuba abakubika buine nge shintililo no kukwata ukuibimba mukusakamana pamo fye nomwenso mukuba abakulanguka nga cakuti kukaba ukupusuka. Ifi fyonse fikwata ukufumya umupashi kuntulo yamaka Yesu. Pela ubusunge bwa mupashi obe kuli Lesa, kabili sumina muli wena. Ulesosa no kutontonkanya pali Yesu. Leka buine bube ubwa kufumishiwapo ukupitila muli wena.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 71, 72.
b. 	Finshi twingakwata ukusambilila Ukufuma mukwalulwa uko ukwakwete ukwisa pa basambi lintu bakwete ukusangwa na Klistu mu mulimo wa butumikishi uwa cilabushiku? Imilimo yaBatumwa 4:13.
“Mukuba abakutwalilila mukulolesha Klistu , tulakwata ukwalulwa mucipasho fye cimo cine Ukufuma ku lulumbi ukuya ku lulumbi ukupitilafye mumupashi wa kwa shikulu..’ 2 Kolinto3:18.
“Eico caishilesangwa ukuti, abasambi bantanshi baishilekwata ukunonka icipasho icakupalana na kapususha wabo uwatemwikwa. Lintu abasambi balekwata ukumfwa amashiwi yakwa Yesu, bakwete ukumfwa ubukabilo bwakwe. Balifwaishe, balisangile, kabili balikwete ukumukonka. bali pamo nankwe mu ng`anda, petebulo, mu muputule, pamofye na mucilime. Bali pamo nankwe ngabana besukulu abali na kafundisha, cilabushiku ukulapokelela ifisambililo fya cine ca mushilo Ukufuma ku milomo yakwe. Baloleshe kuli wena, nga babomfi kuli shikulu wabo, kukusambilila umulimo wabo. Balya abasambi balifye bantu ne myumfwile imo inefye nga ifwebene.  ’ Yakobo 5:17. Balikwete ubulwi bumo bwine ubwakulwisha ulubembu. Balekabila icikuku cimo cine, pakutilafye bengakwanisha ukwikala umweo wa mushilo.”—Ibid., pp. 72, 73.

5. 	A Promise for Us 	Thu, Aug 20
a. 	What wonderful promise has Jesus left for His followers facing the challenges of a hostile world? Matthew 28:20.
“When Christ ascended to Heaven, the sense of His presence was still with His followers. It was a personal presence, full of love and light. Jesus, the Saviour, who had walked and talked and prayed with them, who had spoken hope and comfort to their hearts, had, while the message of peace was still upon His lips, been taken up from them into heaven, and the tones of His voice had come back to them, as the cloud of angels received Him— ‘Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.’ Matthew 28:20.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 73, 74.
b. 	What important instruction did Jesus leave His disciples so they would know what to do in time of need? John 16:23, 24; 14:16–18.
“As they met together after the ascension they were eager to present their requests to the Father in the name of Jesus. . . . They extended the hand of faith higher and higher with the mighty argument, ‘It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.’ Romans 8:34. And Pentecost brought them the presence of the Comforter, of whom Christ had said, He ‘shall be in you.’ And He had further said, ‘It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send Him unto you.’ John 14:17; 16:7. Henceforth through the Spirit, Christ was to abide continually in the hearts of His children. Their union with Him was closer than when He was personally with them. The light, and love, and power of the indwelling Christ shone out through them, so that men, beholding, ‘marveled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.’ Acts 4:13.”—Ibid., pp. 74, 75.
bem:
5. 	UBULAYO KULI BAIFWE                                                            Cisano, Aug 20
a. 	Bulayo nshi ubwa wamisha buntu Yesu akwata ukushila bakakonka bakwe abalekwata ukukumunya amafya ya calo ici icakaluka? Mateo 28:20.
“Lintu Klistu  akwete ukululwa ku mulu, imyumfwile yakubapo kwakwe yali konkenyepo ukuba naba kakonka bakwe. Kwali Ukubapo kwakwe ukwa muli bu muntu, uko ukwaisushiwemo no kutemwa pamofye no lubuto. Yesu, kapususha, uyo uwakwete ukwenda, ukulanda kabili pamofye nokupepa pamo nabo, uyo uwasosele isubilo pamo no kukoselesha ku mitima yabo, alishilekwata ukulwilwa mu mulu pakashita lintu ulusebo lwa mutende lwali lucili pa milomo yakwe, alisendelwe ku mulu ukufumishiwa pakati kabo kabili ne fiunda fye shiwi lyakwe fyakwete ukubwelela kuli bena , ilyo lintu ikumbi lya bangeli lyali ilya ku mupokelela —Ishiwi lyaumfwikike lyali lya kuti ‘Moneni, na kulaba naimwe, ukufikafye na kupwa kwa calo.’ Mateo 28:20.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 73, 74.
b. 	Likambisho nshi ilikankala lintu Yesu akwete ukushila abasambi bakwe pakutila bena bengakwata ukwishiba ico balingile ukucita mu nshita ya kukabila? Yohane 16:23, 24; 14:16–18.
“Lintu bali abakukumana capamo panuma yakululwa bali abafwaisha ukutambika ifyakulomba kwabo kuli Lesa mwishina lyakwa Yesu.  . . . . Balikwete ukutambalika ukuboko kwa citetekelo ukuilakofye pamulu kabili pamulu sana, no kusosa ukwa maka, ukwakuti, ‘Ni Klistu uyo uwa fwile, kabili pa muku umo wine uyo uwakwete ukushukuka kabili uyo uuli ku kuboko kwa kulyo ukwa kwa Lesa, kabili uyo uulekwata ukutupapatilako ifwe.’ Abena Roma 8:34. Kabili pentekositi akwete ukuleta kuli bena ubukota ubo buntu Klistu aeseshe ukulandila kabela ukuti, akakwata ukuba muli imwe. Kabili alikwete ukusosa kuli bene ati, cifwile ukucitika ukuti ine mfwilefye ukuya, pa mulandu wakuti ine nga nshile, ninshi kafwa tekuti abe uwa kwisa, lelo nga cakweba ati naba uwakuya, nkaba uwa kumutuma (kafwa) kuli imwe.’ Yohane 14:17; 16:7. Ukufuma lilya ukuyafye na kuntanshi, ukupitilafye mu mupashi, Klistu ali no kwikala mukutwalilila mu mitima ya bana bakwe. Ubwampano bwabo pamo nankwe bwalishilekwata ukuba ubwa palamisha ukucila fye nelyo ali na bena muli bu muntu. Ulubuto pamo fye no kutemwa elyo na maka ayakubapo kwa kwa Klistu fyakwete ukubalika ukupitila muli bena, pa kutila abantu abalekwata ukubamona, bengaba abakupapuka; kabili baleisa mwikuluka ukuti mucinefye balikwete ukuba na Klistu.” Imilimo ya Batumwa 4:13.”—Ibid., pp. 74, 75

eng:
1. 	The Life and the Light 	Sun, Aug 23
a. 	What is ignored by the natural heart—and with what result? John 1:4, 5.
“God is the source of life and light and joy to the universe. Like rays of light from the sun, like the streams of water bursting from a living spring, blessings flow out from Him to all His creatures. And wherever the life of God is in the hearts of men, it will flow out to others in love and blessing.”—Steps to Christ, p. 77.
b. 	When the love of Christ is cherished in the heart, what will be seen in the life? 2 Corinthians 2:14, 15; 5:14.
“When the love of Christ is enshrined in the heart, like sweet fragrance it cannot be hidden. Its holy influence will be felt by all with whom we come in contact. The spirit of Christ in the heart is like a spring in the desert, flowing to refresh all and making those who are ready to perish, eager to drink of the water of life.”—Ibid., p. 77.
“Let the world see that we are not selfishly absorbed in our own interests, but that we desire others to share our blessings and privileges. Let them see that our religion does not make us unsympathetic or exacting. Let all who profess to have found Christ, minister as He did for the benefit of men.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 152.
bem:
1. 	UMWEO KABILI ULUBUTO 	Cimo, Aug. 26
a. 	Finshi ifyo umutima wa bumuntu ushiposako amano – kabili finshi fifumamo? Yohane 1:4, 5.
“ Lesa entulo ya mweo kabili no lubuto kabili insansa sha mulalo onse. Nge myengelele ukufuma ku kasuba, ngefyo utumana twa menshi utulefuma kukanfuku-nfuku ka Mweo, efyo amapalo yafuma kuli wena ukuya ku fibumbwa fyonse. Kabili uko konse uko umweo wakwa Lesa uli mu mitima ya bantu, uli no kufumina kunse ukuya kuli bambi mukutemwa kabili mwipalo.”—Steps to Christ, p. 77.
b. 	Ilyo ukutemwa kwakwa Klistu kwa bakililwa mu mutima, finshi fili no kumoneka mu mweo? 2 Kolinto 2:14, 15; 5:14.
“Ilyo ukutemwa kwakwa Klistu kwalimbwa mu mutima, nge cena cisuma tekuti kufiswe.  Ulwambu lwakuko ulwa Mushilo luli no kumfwika kuli bonse abo tukumana nabo. Umupashi wakwa Klistu mu mutima waba nga kamfuku-nfuku ka menshi mu ciswebebe, akalepita kuku puputula onse kabili no kuleka bonse abali mukonaika, ukuba abafwaisha ukunwa ko amenshi ya mweo.”—Ibid., p. 77.
“Lekeni icalo cishibe ukuti tatwaba muli bukaitemwe aba kusendwa nefya kutuwamina fye fweka, lelo tulakabila na bambi ukuba aba kukwata icakaniko muma palo elyo na ma shuko yesu. Lekeni bamone ukuti bukapepa bwesu tabutulenga ukuba ababula inkumbu nangula ukuba abashupa. Lekeni onse uutila alisanga Klistu, atumike ngefyo wena atumike ku cinonsho ca Bantu.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 152.

eng:
2. 	Partakers of Grace 	Mon, Aug 24
a. 	When we accept Jesus as our Saviour, what need is supplied? John 1:12, 13; 1 Corinthians 1:4, 5; Romans 5:1, 2.
“Those who are the partakers of the grace of Christ will be ready to make any sacrifice, that others for whom He died may share the heavenly gift. They will do all they can to make the world better for their stay in it. This spirit is the sure outgrowth of a soul truly converted. No sooner does one come to Christ than there is born in his heart a desire to make known to others what a precious friend he has found in Jesus; the saving and sanctifying truth cannot be shut up in his heart. If we are clothed with the righteousness of Christ and are filled with the joy of His indwelling Spirit we shall not be able to hold our peace. If we have tasted and seen that the Lord is good we shall have something to tell. Like Philip when he found the Saviour, we shall invite others into His presence.”—Steps to Christ, p. 78.
b. 	When we are faced with problems and difficulties, what is the counsel of the apostle Paul? Hebrews 4:16.
“Jesus knows the needs of His children, and He loves to listen to their prayers. Let the children shut out the world and everything that would attract the thoughts from God, and let them feel that they are alone with God, that His eye looks into the inmost heart, and reads the desire of the soul, and that they may talk with God.”—Sons and Daughters of God, p. 121.
c. 	Once we become a child of God, what do we owe to others? Romans 1:14, 15.
“In what sense was Paul debtor both to the Jew and to the Greek? To him had been given the commission, as it is given to every disciple of Christ, ‘Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost; teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.’ In accepting Christ, Paul accepted this commission. He realized that upon him rested the obligation of laboring for all classes of men—for Jew and Gentile, learned and unlearned, for those occupying high positions and for those in the most lowly walks of life.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 6, p. 1067.
bem:
2. 	ABAKUMAKO KU CIKUKU 	Cibili, Aug. 24
a. 	Ilyo twapokelela Yesu ngo mupusushi wesu, bushe ca kukabilanshi icipelwa? Yohane 1:12, 13; 1 Korinto 1:4, 5; Roma 5:1, 2.
“Bonse aba kumako ku cikuku cakwa Klistu bakaba aba ipekanya ukuba aba kuipela bulilambo, pakuti na bambi ebo afwilile bengakwata icakaniko mu ca bupe ca kumulu. Bakacita conse ico bengakwanisha pakuti bengapanga icalo ukuba icisuma sana ico bena bengekalamo. Uyu mupashi caba cintu cifuma mumweo uwapilibuka mucishinka. Lilya line fye umo aisa kuli Klistu mu mutima wakwe mulafyalwa ukukabilisha ukwakulenga bambi beshibe ifyo awama cibusa uo asanga muli Yesu; icishinka icakupususha kabili icakushisha tekuti cisalilwe [cifiswe] mu mutima wakwe. Nga cakuti twafwikwa ubololoke bwakwa Klistu kabili twaisushiwamo ne nsansa sha mupashi wakwe uwaikala mukati tatwakekale tondolo. Nga cakuti na tumona kabili no kusonda ukuti Shikulu musuma tuli no kukwata fimo ifya kushimika. Ngefyo cali kuli Filipi ilyo asangile umupusushi, tuli no kulalikako na bambi kuli wena.”—Steps to Christ, p. 78.
b. 	Ilyo twakumanya amafya kabili ne fyakosa, ni bumpanda mano nshi ubo umusole Paulo apela? Abahebere4:16.
“Yesu alishiba ifyo abana bakwe bakabila, kabili alitemwa ukumfwa ku mapepo yabo. Lekeni abana besalile kunse icalo pamo na conse icingongola amatontokanyo yabo ukubafumya kuli Lesa, kabili lekeni bena bomfwe ukuti balifye beka na Lesa, no kutila ilinso lyakwe limona mukati ka mutima, kabili abalenga ukukabila kwa mupashi, kabili ukuti bengalanda na Lesa.”—Sons and Daughters of God, p. 121.
c. 	Ilyofye twaba umwana wakwa Lesa, bushe mishanshi tu kwata kuli bambi? Roma 1:14, 15.
“Bushe ni mushila nshi emo Paulo abelele uwamisha kuba Yuda na Kuba Greeki? Kuli wena kwalipelwe umulimo, ngefyo fye wapelwa ku musambi wakwa Klistu onse, ‘eico kabiyeni, no kusambilisha inko shonse, mulebabatisha Mwishina lyakwa tata, umwna elyo no Mupashi wa mushilo; ukubakambisha ukubaka fyonse ifyo na mwebele ukucita: Kabili, moneni, ndinenu lyonse ukufika na ku kupwa kwa calo.’mukupokelela Klistu, Paulo asumine uyu mulimo. Akutulwike ukuti alikwete umulimo uwa kutumikila ama bumba yabantu yonse—aba yuda elyo nabena fyalo, abasambilila na bashasambilila, abafifulo ifya pamulu kabili pamofye na babesha pesamba mu bwikashi bwa mweo.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 6, p. 10

eng:
3. 	Fruit of Conversion 	Tue, Aug 25
a. 	If the Holy Spirit is in our hearts, what will be one of our first actions? John 1:41, 42.
“We shall seek to present to [others] the attractions of Christ and the unseen realities of the world to come. There will be an intensity of desire to follow in the path that Jesus trod. There will be an earnest longing that those around us may ‘behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.’ John 1:29.
“And the effort to bless others will react in blessings upon ourselves. This was the purpose of God in giving us a part to act in the plan of redemption. He has granted men the privilege of becoming partakers of the divine nature and, in their turn, of diffusing blessings to their fellow men. This is the highest honor, the greatest joy, that it is possible for God to bestow upon men. Those who thus become participants in labors of love are brought nearest to their Creator.
“God might have committed the message of the gospel, and all the work of loving ministry, to the heavenly angels. He might have employed other means for accomplishing His purpose. But in His infinite love He chose to make us coworkers with Himself, with Christ and the angels, that we might share the blessing, the joy, the spiritual uplifting, which results from this unselfish ministry.
We are brought into sympathy with Christ through the fellowship of His sufferings. Every act of self-sacrifice for the good of others strengthens the spirit of beneficence in the giver’s heart, allying him more closely to the Redeemer of the world, who ‘was rich, yet for your sakes. . . . became poor, that ye through His poverty might be rich.’ 2 Corinthians 8:9. And it is only as we thus fulfill the divine purpose in our creation that life can be a blessing to us.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 78–80.
b. 	What example of Christ should guide us in our relationships with relatives and neighbors? Galatians 6:9, 10; John 9:4.
“If you will go to work as Christ designs that His disciples shall, and win souls for Him, you will feel the need of a deeper experience and a greater knowledge in divine things, and will hunger and thirst after righteousness. You will plead with God, and your faith will be strengthened, and your soul will drink deeper drafts at the well of salvation. Encountering opposition and trials will drive you to the Bible and prayer. You will grow in grace and the knowledge of Christ, and will develop a rich experience.”—Ibid., p. 80.
bem:
3. 	ICISABO CAKUPILIBUKA 	Citatu, Aug. 25
a. 	Nga cakuti umupashi wa mushilo uli mu mitima yesu, bushe cishi ico tuli no kubalilapo ukucita? Yohane 1:41, 42.
“Tukafwaya ukulangisha [kuli bambi] ifya longolo fyakwa Klistu kabili ne fyacine ifishimonwa ifya mucalo icileisa. Kuli no kuba ukukabila ukukalamba ukwakufwaya ukukonka inshila umo Yesu aendele.  Kukaba ukukabila ukwacishinka ukwa kuti abo aba tushingulwike ‘bamone umwana wa mpanga uwakwa Lesa.’ Yohane 1:29.
“Kabili ukufwaisha ukupala bambi kukaleta amapalo pali fwebene. Uku ekwali ukufwaya kwakwa Lesa ilyo atupele ulubali ulwa kubombamo mu mutande we pusukilo. Alipela ishuko ku bantu ilya kuba aba kukumako kumubele wa buLesa, kabili no kupelako amapalo ku bantu banabo.   Uyu mucinshi uwa sumbukisha, insansa isha kulisha, isho Lesa engakwata ukubiba pa bantu. Abo bonse aba sendamo ulubali mukubomba kwa kutemwa balapalamikwa mupepi sana na kabumba.
“Lesa nga alipele ku bangeli ba kumulu umulimo wa mbila nsuma, kabili no mulimo onse uwa butumikishi bwa kutemwa. Kabili nga alibonfeshe inshila shimbi isha kupwishishishamo ubufwayo bwakwe. Lelo mukutemwa kwakwe ukushipwa [ukwakulisha] asalile ukutupanga ifwe aba kubombela pamo nankwe, pamo na Klistu elyo na bangeli, pakutlai twingakwatako icakaniko mu mapalo, mu nsansa, kabili na mukusumbulwa kwa kuli bumupashi, ifyo ififuma mu butumikishi umushaba bu kaitemwe.
Tulakwata ukuletwa mu nkumbu pamo na Klistu ukupitila mukwampana [mukukumako] mukucula kwakwe. Icicitwa conse icakuipela bulilambo pa mulandu wa busuma bwa bambi cikosha bukapekape mu mutima wakwa kapela, ukumupalamika mupepi kuli kapususha wa calo, uwali uwa fyuma, lelo pa mulandu obe…… ashileba umupina, pakuti iwe ukupitila mu bupina bwakwe wingaba umukankala.’ 2 Korinto 8:9. Kabili nilyo fye twafikilisha ubufwayo bwakwa Lesa mu bubumbo bwesu elyo umweo wesu wingaba lipalo kuli ifwe.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 78–80.
b. 	Bushe cakumwenako nshi icakwa Klistu icifwile ukututungulula ifwe pafyo twingekala ne ndupwa shesu elyo na bena mu palamano? Galatia 6:9, 10; Yohane 9:4.
“ Nga cakuti waile mu kubomba ukulingana nefyo Klistu acibikile ukuti abasambi bakwe bafwile ukucita, kabili no kunonka imipashi kuli wena, ukomfwa ukukabila ukwacibelesho icashika elyo no kwiluka ukwakulisha mu fintu fya buLesa, kabili ukomfwa icilaka elyo ne nsala ya bulungami. Ikalilila muli Lesa, kabili icitetekelo cobe cikakoseleshiwa, kabili umupashi obe ukanwa amenshi ayengi pa cishima ce pusukilo. Uku kumanya ukupilikwa kabili na mesho fikakutwala ku cipingo elyo ne pepo. Ukakula mu cikuku kabili no kwishiba Klistu, kabili ukakwata icibelesho icashika.”—Ibid., p. 80.

eng:
4. 	Unselfish Work 	Wed, Aug 26
a. 	Name one great danger for us as members of the church today. Malachi 3:8–10.
“At present [Sabbathkeeping Adventists’] greatest danger is in their accumulations of property. Some are continually increasing their cares and labors; they are overcharged. The result is, God and the wants of His cause are nearly forgotten by them; they are spiritually dead. They are required to make a sacrifice to God, an offering. A sacrifice does not increase, but decreases and consumes. . . . Much of the means among our people is only proving an injury to those who are holding on to it.”—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 1, p. 492.
b. 	What Christian virtues help believers develop in grace and knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ? 1 Peter 4:8–10; Hebrews 13:2.
“The privilege granted Abraham and Lot is not denied to us. By showing hospitality to God’s children we, too, may receive His angels into our dwellings. Even in our day, angels in human form enter the homes of men and are entertained by them. And Christians who live in the light of God’s countenance are always accompanied by unseen angels, and these holy beings leave behind them a blessing in our homes.”—Ibid., vol. 6, p. 342.
c. 	What need must be filled by believers today? 2 Corinthians 10:16.
“The lay members of our churches can accomplish a work which, as yet, they have scarcely begun. None should move into new places merely for the sake of worldly advantage; but where there is an opening to obtain a livelihood, let families that are well grounded in the truth enter, one or two families in a place, to work as missionaries. They should feel a love for souls, a burden of labor for them, and should make it a study how to bring them into the truth. They can distribute our publications, hold meetings in their homes, become acquainted with their neighbors, and invite them to come to these meetings. Thus they can let their light shine in good works.”—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 8, p. 245.
“Long has God waited for the spirit of service to take possession of the whole church so that everyone shall be working for Him according to his ability. When the members of the church of God do their appointed work in the needy fields at home and abroad, in fulfillment of the gospel commission, the whole world will soon be warned and the Lord Jesus will return to this earth with power and great glory.”—The Acts of the Apostles, p. 111.
bem:
4. 	UMULIMO UWABULA BUKAITEMWE 	Cine, Aug. 26
a. 	Lumbulapo ubusanso bumo ubukalamba ubuli kuli ifwe nge filundwa fya cilonganino. Malaki 3:8–10.
“Pali nomba [Bakalolela abasunga isabata’] ubusanso ubukulisha buli mu kufusha [uku kolonganya] ifikwatwa. Bambi balafusha ifya kusakamana kabili no kubombesha; balatitikishiwa apakalamba. Icifumamo cakuti, Lesa pamofye ne fifwaikwa mu mulimo wakwe filakwata ukulabwa kuli aba bantu; balifwa kuli bu mupashi.  Balefwaikwa ukupela ilambo kuli Lesa, icabupe. Ilambo talikulilako lelo lilacepelako elyo nokupwa……indalama ishingi pakati ka bantu besu shiletafye ukucena kuli abo baleshikatilila.”—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 1, p. 492.
b. 	Bushe busuma nshi ubwa bwina Klistu ubwafwilisha abasumini ukukula mu cikuku kabili mukwiluka [mukwishiba] kwakwa shikulu Yesu Klistu? 1 Petelo 4:8–10; aba Hebele 13:2.
“Ishuko ilyapelwe kuli Abramu tabatutana ifwe. Ukupitila mukutangata abana bakwa Lesa, naifwe bene, kuti twapokelela bamalaika mu mayanda yesu. Na mu nshita yesu, ba malaika mu musango wa bantu balengila mu mayanda ya bantu kabili balabapokelela. Kabili abena Klistu abekala ku cinso cakwa Lesa lyonse baba na bangeli aba shimoneka, kabili ifi fibumbwa fya mushilo filasha ipalo mu mayanda yesu.”—Ibid., vol. 6, p. 342.
c. 	Bushe cakukabila nshi ico abasumini ba pali nomba bafwile ukufikilisha? 2 Korinto 10:16.
“Ifilundwa fya filonganino fyesu kuti fyapwishishisha umulimo uo, ba tendekefye pali nomba. Tapali nangu umo uu fwile ukuya mu ncende ishipya pa mulandu fye wa busuma bwa mu calo; lelo mu ncende umwingasangwa ubwikashi, lekeni ulupwa lumo nangula shibili, isha limbwa bwino mu cine bengile mu ncende, mu kubomba nga ba minshoni.  Bafwile ukutemwa imipashi, uyu e mulimo untu bafwile ukubomba bena, kabili bafwile ukusambilila efyo bengabaleta ku cine. Kuti basabankanya impapulo shesu, kuti bakwata ukulanshanya mu mayanda yabo, kabili kuti bakwata ukwishibana na bena mu palamano babo, kabili no ku balalika ukwisa ku kukumana [ku kulanshanya] uku. Mu kucita ifi kuti balenga ulubuto lwa balikila mu milimo isuma.”—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 8, p. 245.
“Lesa alilolela panshite ntali ukuti umupashi wa kubomba wingatungulula icilonganino conse pakutila onse engamubombela ukulingana napo engapelela. Ilyo ifilundwa fya mu cilonganino cakwa Lesa fyabomba umulimo wapelwa mu mabala umuli ukukabila mu ncende bekalamo nangula mufyalo fimbi, mukufishapo umulimo ukalamba uwa kushimikila, icalo conse cilino kusokwa mukwangufyanya kabili shikulu Yesu Klistu ali no kubwela pa calo cino no lupaka kabili no lulumbi ulukalamba.”—The Acts of the Apostles, p. 111.

eng:
5. 	Faithful Representatives 	Thu, Aug 27
a. 	What is expected of all those entrusted with the Gospel—and especially the workers? 1 Corinthians 4:1, 2; Revelation 2:10.
“It is the privilege of the watchmen on the walls of Zion to live so near to God, and to be so susceptible to the impressions of His Spirit, that He can work through them to tell sinners of their peril, and point them to the place of safety. Chosen of God, sealed with the blood of consecration, they are to rescue men and women from impending destruction. Faithfully are they to warn their fellowmen of the sure result of transgression, and faithfully are they to safeguard the interest of the church.”—Gospel Workers, p. 15.
b. 	What example did Daniel set for today’s youth? Daniel 1:8, 15.
“The Lord would have us learn a lesson also from the experience of Daniel. There are many who might become mighty men if like this faithful Hebrew they would depend upon God for grace to be overcomers, and for strength and efficiency in their labors. Daniel manifested the most perfect courtesy, both toward his elders and toward the youth. He stood as a witness for God, and sought to take such a course that he might not be ashamed for heaven to hear his words or to behold his works. When Daniel was required to partake of the luxuries of the king’s table, he did not fly into a passion, neither did he express a determination to eat and drink as he pleased. Without speaking one word of defiance, he took the matter to God. He and his companions sought wisdom from the Lord, and when they came forth from earnest prayer their decision was made. With true courage and Christian courtesy, Daniel presented the case to the officer who had them in charge, asking that they might be granted a simple diet. These youth felt that their religious principles were at stake, and they relied upon God, whom they loved and served.”—Testimonies to Ministers, p. 263.
bem:
5. 	ABEMINISHI BA CISHINKA 	Cisano, Aug. 27
a. 	Finshi balingile ukucita abo aba pelwa imbila nsuma—maka maka ababomfi? 1 Korinto 4:1, 2; Kusokolola 2:10.
“Lyaliba lishuko lyakwa kalinda wa fibumba fya Zioni ukwikala mupepi na Lesa, kabili no kuba uwa kutungululwa no mupashi wakwe, pakuti ukupitila muli bena engaba uwakweba aba bembu ubusanso bwaba mukutoba ifunde, kabili no kubasontelela kucifulo ca bucingo. Abasalwa bakwa Lesa, aba komenenwa no mulopa wa kushisha, bafwile ukupususha abaume na banakashi ku bonaushi ubuleisa. Muli bucishinka bafwile ukusoka abantu banabo icifuma mukutoba kwefunde, kabili bafwile ukubakilila ubukankala bwa cilonganino.”—Gospel Workers, p. 15.  Interest
b.  Bushe Daniele ca kumwenako nshi apele ku bapungwe ba pali lelo? Daniele 1:8, 15.
“Shikulu kuti aleka ifwe ukusambililako icibelesho ukufuma kuli Daniele. Bengi abengaba abaume aba bulamba nga uyu umu Hebele wa cishinka nga cakuti ba shintile pali Lesa ukuti bengaba ne cikuku icakubapela bukacimfya, no kukoshiwa kabili no kuba abafikapo mu mibombele yabo.  Daniele alangishe umucisnshi uwafikapo, kuba kalamba kabili na kubapungwe. Aiminine ngente yakwa Lesa, kabili afwaishe no kusenda inshila iya kuti tekuti abe uwa kulengwa insoni elyo umulu waumfwa amashiwi yakwe nangula ukumona imilimo yakwe. Ilyo Daniele ba mwitile ukulya kwitebulo lya mfumu ilya malila, talangishe insuna, kabili talangishe ukufwaisha ukulya elyo no kunwa mu kuisekesha.  Ukwabula ukusosa ishiwi ilya misuula, atwele umulandu kuli Lesa. Ena pamofye nebo ali nabo balombele amano ukufuma kuli Lesa, kabili ilyo ba fumine mwipepo ilya cishinka ubusalo bwabo bwali pangilwe. No kupama ukwa cishinka kabili mu mucinshi uwa bwina Klistu, Daniele atwele umulandu wakwe kuli cilolo uwalebamonapo, alombele ukuti ifyakulya fyabo fibefye ifya yanguka. Abapungwe baumfwile ukuti ifipope fya bukapepa bwabo fyali mukayofi [mubwafya], kabili bashintilile pali Lesa, uo ba temenwe kabili no kutumika.”—Testimonies to Ministers, p. 263.

eng:
Personal Review Questions 	Fri, Aug 28
1. 	What condition of the world made it necessary for God to infuse light into it?
2. 	What marvelous change will be seen in the life of believers?
3. 	When a blessing is received, what should be the response?
4. 	Describe some ways by which each of us can serve others.
5. 	How is Daniel’s faithfulness an inspiration to me?
First Sabbath Offering
September 5, 2026
Bible Missionary Training School in the Philippines
As we are reminded of the great commission to go into all the world and make disciples, we are to take action. The Bible Missionary Training School is an institution dedicated to preparing and equipping workers for the Lord’s vineyard. Since its founding in February 1984, this school has been a beacon of faith, shaping the hearts and minds of those eager to spread the gospel to all nations. Many students who have completed the two-year missionary training program this institution offers have gone on to become missionaries abroad, and several are leaders and ministers spreading the message of salvation throughout the densely populated islands of the Philippines.
Located in Cabatang, Tiaong, Quezon Province, Philippines, the Bible Missionary Training School has tirelessly worked to provide a solid biblical foundation for aspiring missionaries both in the Philippines and throughout the Pacific Region. This facility has provided a place for students to stay, learn English and to be trained as missionaries, canvassers, health workers and administrators so greatly needed in this country and abroad. It has also served as a facility where training seminars, youth conventions, and conferences can be held.
As the work of reformation has grown throughout the Philippines, expansion and improvements of this facility are now urgently needed so it can continue to serve the needs of God’s cause going forward. In light of these needs, plans are also underway to hold a General Conference Session right here at this very institution. What a blessing it would be to host this gathering of believers, where visions for evangelism and spiritual revival will take center stage!
Your generous First Sabbath School Offering today will be instrumental in building the much-needed expansion for this institution. As we give, let us remember the words of 2 Corinthians 9:7, “Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.”
May your gifts uplift this school, empower its mission, and bring forth workers ready to proclaim the everlasting gospel. Let us give with faith and joy, knowing that our contributions will bear eternal fruits for God’s kingdom.
Thank you, and may the Lord bless you abundantly as you give!
Your brethren in the Philippines
