Ubupe Bwe Sabata Lya Ntanshi
Ulusuba Lunono 5, 2026
Isukulu lya ku kampushishapo ba Kabomba ba Chipingo mu Philippines
Nge fyo tuleba aba kwibukishiwako pa ku tumwa ukwa kuya ku calo conse kabili no kupanga abasambi, tufwile twakwata ukwima no kubomba. Isukulu lya ku kampushishapo ba Kabomba ba Chipingo yaliba ni ncende iya sontwa mu kupekanishisha no kupangasha [ukulongelesha] ababomfi ku kubomba mwi bala lya myangashi. Ukufuma fye apo balyabile mu mwaka wa 1984 mukabengele kanono ili isukulu lyaliba cisontelelo ca citeyekelo, mu kwalula imitima na malangulushi ya abo sbakwata ukufwaisha kwa kusabankanya imbila nsuma kunko shonse. Abengi aba kwata ukukampushiwa pa imyaka ibili iya masambililo yantu ili isukulu lipela lya minshoni bali twalilila ukya mu kuba ba missioni ku fyalo fya kutali, kabii abengi bali ni ntungullushi kabili bambi bakakumba mukusabankanya imbila ye pusukilo mu fishi ifya fulamo abantu ifya panga icalo ca Philippine.
Ili isukulu lya ku kampusha ukwa cipingo ilyabela mu citungu [province] ca Cabatang, Tiaong, Quezon, mu calo ca Philippines   lya likwata mu ku twalilila ukuboma mukubika umufula uwakosa uwa kukoselesha ba missioni  muli ifi ifishi fya Philippines pamo pene ne ncende fye yonse iya Pacific. Ili isukulu lyali pela incende ya kwikalako abasambi, ukusambililaicisungu pamo pene no ku kampushiwa ng aba minshoni, ba kashitisha wa mpapulo [ba Cuma milamba], ba kabomba ba ku fya pamo fye bundapishi   na bakatungula ba mufipanifya mu mubombole abo ababa aba fwaikwa sana muli ici icalo pamo pene fyene fya kutali. Kabili ya lya fwilisha mukuba nge ncende iya kukampushishapo ukupitila  mu ma semina, ukulongana kwa bapunwe, no kutekelwapo ifilye ifikalamba ifya filonganino.
Pa mulandu wa kutila umulimo wa kufukulula na ukwata uukufunguluka mu ncende ya calo ca Philippines, ukukusha no kuwamya iyi ncende kule fwaikwa mu kwa ngufyanya pa kutila inga twalilila ukukwanisha kwa makabilo  ya mulimo wakwa Lesa uyo uletwalilila ukuya pantanshi. Pa ku kwata ukumona aya ma bukabilo, amanshiko  eko yali aya kwisa kwatila uku kumana kwa cisaka cikalamba kuno kwine pali iyi ine ncende ye sukulu. We palo we ilili no kwisaba mu mukuba bakapokelela wa basumini aba kakwata ukukolongana, uko kuntu ifimonwa fya kusabankanya kwa mbila nsuma no ku puputulwa kwa kuli bu mupashi kuli no ku kwatila ukubela!
Ukupelesha kwenu ukwa bupe bwe sabata lya ntanshi ilya lelo kuli no kuba nge cibombelo mu kukula uko ukulekabilwa sana mu kukusha kwa ili sukulu. Ilyo mulekwata ukupela, muleibukisha ama  shiwi ya muli   2 Korinto 9:7 “Umuntu onse apele ukulingana ne fyo apingile mu mutima wakwe, ukwabula ukuilishanya, lelo mu kuitemenwa: pantu Lesa atemwa kapela wa kwanga [uwansansa].”
Lekene ifya bupe fyenu fikwate ukutwala pa ntanshi ili isukulu, tungilileni umulimo waliko, mu kulilenga ukulafunyapo ababomfi abo ababa abaipekanya ukusabankanya imbila nsuma ya muyayaya. Natukwate ukupela kanshi mu citetekelo ne nsansa, mu kwishiba ukutila ama bupe yesu yali no kuleta ifisabo fya muyayaya ku bufumu bwakwa Lesa.
Twatasha, kabili shikulu e ngamupala apakalamba elyo mulekwata ukupela!
Ba munyinenwe mu calo ca Philippines

eng:
1. 	God Reveals Himself 	Sun, Aug 30
a. 	By what things in this world is the Lord seeking to draw men to Himself? Psalm 19:1–6; Proverbs 2:1–5.
“Many are the ways in which God is seeking to make Himself known to us and bring us into communion with Him. Nature speaks to our senses without ceasing. The open heart will be impressed with the love and glory of God as revealed through the works of His hands. The listening ear can hear and understand the communications of God through the things of nature. The green fields, the lofty trees, the buds and flowers, the passing cloud, the falling rain, the babbling brook, the glories of the heavens, speak to our hearts, and invite us to become acquainted with Him who made them all.”—Steps to Christ, p. 85.
b. 	What did Jesus use to fix truth in the minds of His hearers? Matthew 13:3, 34.
“Our Saviour bound up His precious lessons with the things of nature. The trees, the birds, the flowers of the valleys, the hills, the lakes, and the beautiful heavens, as well as the incidents and surroundings of daily life, were all linked with the words of truth, that His lessons might thus be often recalled to mind, even amid the busy cares of man’s life of toil.
“God would have His children appreciate His works and delight in the simple, quiet beauty with which He has adorned our earthly home.”—Ibid.
bem:
1. 	LESA ALAISOKOLOLA UMWINE 	Cimo, Sept. 30
a. 	Kupitila mu fintu nshi muno calo e mo Shikulu alefwaila ukupalamikila abantu kuli wena? Malumbo 19:1–6; Mapinda 2:1–5.
"Inshila shingi umo Lesa alefwaila ukuisokolola kuli baifwe kabili no kutwampanya kuli wena. Ububumbo busosa kuli kampingu wesu ukwabula ukuleka. Umutima uwaisuka ukasekeshiwa no kutemwa kabili no lulumbi lwakwa Lesa ngefyo lwa sokololwa ukupitila mu milimo ya maboko yakwe.  Ukutwi ukumfwa kuti kwakutika kabili no kwishiba ukulanshanya kwakwa Lesa ukupitila mu fintu ifya bu bumbo. Amabala aya katapa-katapa [aya funda], imiti iyitali, amaluba aya balula, amakumbi aya pita, imfula iiloka, umukuku wa menshi ayalepita, ululumbi lwa myulu, filanda ku mitima yesu, kabili filatulalika ukuya kuku mwishiba   uyo uwa pangile fyonse ifi.”—Steps to Christ, p. 85.
b. 	Bushe Yesu cinshi ico abomfeshe pa kupampamika icine mu mano ya bakomfwa bakwe? Mateo 13:3, 34.
“Umupusushi wesu alibika ifisambililo fyakwe ifisuma mu fya bubumbo. Ifimuti, ifyuni, amaluba yamu malungu, ifimana, kabili ne myulu iisuma, ukubikapofye ne fintu ifitushinguluka mu bwikashi bwesu ubwa cila bushiku, fyonse fyali ifya suntinkana na mashiwi ya cine, pakuti ukupitila muli ifi ifisambililo fyakwe fileba ifya kwibuskishiwa mu malangulushi lyonse, nangufye mukusakamana kwa kupikintinka kwa mibombele ya mu mweo wa muntu.
“Lesa afwaya abana bakwe ukutasha imilimo yakwe kabili no ku cankwa mu musango uwayanguka, mu busuma  ubwa tondolo ifyo efyo abika mu ng’anda yesu iya calo.”—Ibid.

eng:
2. 	God’s Created Works 	Mon, Aug 31
a. 	What lesson may be learned from nature—for example in the flowers, birds, and stars? Romans 1:20; Acts 14:17.
“In the study of the sciences . . . we are to obtain a knowledge of the Creator. All true science is but an interpretation of the handwriting of God in the material world. Science brings from her research only fresh evidences of the wisdom and power of God. Rightly understood, both the book of nature and the written word make us acquainted with God by teaching us something of the wise and beneficent laws through which He works.”—Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 599.
“If we will but listen, God’s created works will teach us precious lessons of obedience and trust. From the stars that in their trackless courses through space follow from age to age their appointed path, down to the minutest atom, the things of nature obey the Creator’s will. And God cares for everything and sustains everything that He has created.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 85, 86.
b. 	When we contemplate the beauty and peace of unspoiled nature, what should be remembered of the promised new earth? 1 Corinthians 2:9; Revelation 21:1.
“Let your imagination picture the home of the saved, and remember that it will be more glorious than your brightest imagination can portray. In the varied gifts of God in nature we see but the faintest gleaming of His glory.”—Ibid., pp. 86, 87.
“The church of God has been given revelations of the eternal purpose of Jehovah. His people have been permitted to look beyond the trials of the present to the triumphs of the future, when, the warfare having been accomplished, the redeemed will enter into possession of the promised land. These visions of future glory, scenes pictured by the hand of God, should be dear to His church today.”—Prophets and Kings, p. 722.
“In the Bible the inheritance of the saved is called ‘a country.’ Hebrews 11:14–16. There the heavenly Shepherd leads His flock to fountains of living waters. The tree of life yields its fruit every month, and the leaves of the tree are for the service of the nations. There are ever-flowing streams, clear as crystal, and beside them waving trees cast their shadows upon the paths prepared for the ransomed of the Lord. There the wide-spreading plains swell into hills of beauty, and the mountains of God rear their lofty summits. On those peaceful plains, beside those living streams, God’s people, so long pilgrims and wanderers, shall find a home.”—The Great Controversy, p. 675.
bem:
2. 	IMILIMO YA BUMBILWE NA LESA 	Cimo, Aug. 31
a. 	Cisambililo nshi ico twingaba aba kusambililako ku filengwa na Lesa—ukufuma ku maluba, ifyuni kabili ne ntanda? Roma 1:20; Acts 14:17.
“Mukusambilila kwa mufya kufwailisha (sciences) . . . tuli no kunonkamo ukwishiba kwakwa kabumba. Fyonse ifya kufwailisha fya bafye kwilula (kupilibula) kwafyo Lesa alemba no kuboko mu fintu fya mucalo. Ifya kufwailisha (sciences) filetafye ifyaku shininkishishako ifipya ifya mano kabili na maka yakwa Lesa ukufuma mukufwilimfwintwa [mukufwailishiwa] kwafiko. Ilyo twa fyumfwikisha bwino fyonse ifitabo fibili elyo ne cebo icalembwa fitulenga ukwishiba Lesa ukupitila mu kutufundisha fimo ifya wa mano kabili na mafunde ayalete cinonsho umo muntu abombela.”—Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 599.
“Nga cakuti twinga kwata  uku kutika, imilimo ya bubumbo bwakwa Lesa ikatufundisha ifisambililo ifikankala ifya cumfwila kabili no kucetekela. Ukufuma fye kuntanda isho ishishakwata inshila lelo shikonka umwakupita umwapelwa ukufuma kunkulo ne nkulo, ukufikafye na ku kantu akacepesha, ifintu fya bubumbo fibeela ubufwayo bwakwa Kabumba. Kabili Lesa asakamana no kutungilila conse ico abumba.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 85, 86.
Ilyo twatontonkanya pa kuyemba elyo no mutende wa bubumbo ubushaonaulwa, finshi tufwile ukwibukisha pa cikumine icalo icipya icalailwe? 1 Korinto 2:9; Ukusokolola 21:1.
“Lekeni ukwelenganya kwenu kupashanye ing’anda yaba pusushiwa, kabili ibukisheni ukuti cikaba icapulamisha ukucila nefyo mu celenganya. Mubwingi bwa fyabupe fyakwa Lesa ifya bubumbo ifya lekana-lekana tumonamo fye akashiminishi ka lulumbi lwakwe.”—Ibid., pp. 86, 87.
“Icilonganino cakwa Lesa calipelwa ukusokolola kwa bufwayo bwakwa Yohova ubwa muyayaya. Abantu bakwe balisumunishiwa ukulolesha ukupula pa mesho ayapali lelo ukulola kukucimfya ukwa kuntanshi, ilyo, ubulwi na bupwishishiwa, abalubulwa bakengila mufikwatwa fya mucifulo icalailwe. Ifi ifimonwa ifya lulumbi ululeisa, ifikacitika ifyalondololwa no kuboko kwakwa Lesa, fifwile ukuba ifya temwikwa [ifikankala] ku cilonganino cakwe ilelo.”—Prophets and Kings, p. 722.
“Mucipingo, icabupyani ca balubulwa  citwa ‘icalo. BaHebele 11:14–16. Mulya kacema wa mu mulu atungulula umukuni wakwe ku kamfukumfuku ka menshi ya mweo. Icimuti ca mweo citwala ifisabo fyaciko cila mweshi, kabili na mabula ya cimuti kukundapa inko. Kwaba utumana utupila pe, utwa lengama, kabili pambali yatuko ifimuti ifilepungaila fibika icintelelwe kutushila utwapekanishiwila aba lubulwa bakwa shikulu. Kulya amalungu aya funguluka mwaba utupili utwayemba, kabili ne mpili shakwa Lesa shilangisha ukulepa kwa shiko.  Pa aya amalungu aya mutende, pambali ya tumana utwa mweo, Abantu bakwa Lesa, abali abalebeshi kabili abalubanta pa nshite ntali, bakasanga [ubwikalo] ing’anda.”—The Great Controversy, p. 675

eng:
3. 	The Witness of Providence 	Tue, Sep 1
a. 	What precious lessons may be learned from the prophets to encourage us in times of discouragement and temptation? James 5:17; Romans 8:28; 1 John 5:14.
“In our circumstances and surroundings, in the changes daily taking place around us, we may find precious lessons if our hearts are but open to discern them. . . .  [The patriarchs and prophets] men ‘subject to like passions as we are.’ James 5:17. We see how they struggled through discouragements like our own, how they fell under temptation as we have done, and yet took heart again and conquered through the grace of God; and, beholding, we are encouraged in our striving after righteousness.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 87, 88.
b. 	If God provides for the things of nature, how much more for His children? Psalms 107:43; 145:15, 16.
“Nature and revelation alike testify of God’s love. Our Father in heaven is the source of life, of wisdom, and of joy. Look at the wonderful and beautiful things of nature. Think of their marvelous adaptation to the needs and happiness, not only of man, but of all living creatures. The sunshine and the rain, that gladden and refresh the earth, the hills and seas and plains, all speak to us of the Creator’s love.”—Ibid., p. 9.
c. 	On what should the promise of God’s care lead us to focus? Matthew 6:30–34.
“When we take into our hands the management of things with which we have to do, and depend upon our own wisdom for success, we are taking a burden which God has not given us, and are trying to bear it without His aid. We are taking upon ourselves the responsibility that belongs to God, and thus are really putting ourselves in His place. We may well have anxiety and anticipate danger and loss, for it is certain to befall us. But when we really believe that God loves us and means to do us good we shall cease to worry about the future. We shall trust God as a child trusts a loving parent. Then our troubles and torments will disappear, for our will is swallowed up in the will of God.”—Thoughts from the Mount of Blessing, pp. 100, 101.
bem:
3. 	INTE YA PA FINTU IFICITIKA 	 Citatu, Sept 1
a. 	Fisambililo nshi ifikankala ifyapita ifyo twingasambililako kuli bakasesema mukukoselesha ifwe mu nshita sha kunashiwa elyo no kutunkwa? Yakobo 5:17; Roma 8:28; 1 Yohane 5:14.
“Mufitucitikila kabili nefya tushinguluka mukupilibuka [kwafintu] ificitikila cilabushishu mukushinguluka, kuti twamonamo ifisambililo ifikankala nga cakutifye imitima yesu shaisuka no kufimona…. [ bakasesema ne fikolwe] abantu aba myumfwilefye ngaifwe ‘Yakobo 5:17. Tulakwata ukumona ifyo bakwete ukucucutika ukupitila mukunashiwa, nefyo bakwete ukuwa mumatunko ngefyo naifwe bene ciba, nomba balekwata ukwima kabili no kucinfya na kabili ukupitila mu cikuku cakwa Lesa; kabili, na mukukwata ukumona tulakwata uku koseleshiwa mu kulwisha kwesu ukwakufika ku bulungami.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 87, 88.
b. 	Nga cakuti Lesa alapela ifyo ifya bubumbo [ifilengwa na Lesa] fikabila, bushe tekuti apele ukucilamo kubana bakwe? Malumbo 107:43; 145:15, 16.
“Ububumbo elyo no busokololo fipela ubunte pa kutemwa kwakwa Lesa. Shifwe wa mu mulu entulo ya mweo, amano, kabili ne nsasa. Lolesheni pa fyakupapusha kabili ifyayemba ifya bubumbo. Tontonkanyenipo pafyo fyaba ifyakukwanisha ifya mabukabilo kabili ne nsansa, te fya muntu fye, ne fintu fyonse ifya mweo. Ukubalika kwa kasuba elyo ne mfula, ifikwata ukusansamusha noku puputula icalo, utupili, babemba elyo na malungu, fyonse filanda palwa ukutemwa kwakwa Kalenga.”—Ibid., p. 9.
Ni pali cinshi epo ubulayo bwa kusakamana kwakwa Lesa bwinga tutungulula ukulolekeshapo? Mateo 6:30–34.
“Nga cakuti twasendela mu minwe yesu imibombele ya fintu ifyo tufwile ukucita, kabili no kushintililla pa mano yesu fye fwebene pa kupwishishisha, tulesenda icisendo ico Lesa tatupela, kabili tule-esha ukucisenda ukwabula ubwafwilisho bwakwe. Tulebika pali fwebene umulimo uyo uuli wakwa Lesa, kabili na munshila iyi tuleibika pa cifulo cakwe. Kuti twaba aba kusakamana kabili no kusubila ubusanso elyo no kulufya, pa mulandu wakutila cili icashininkishiwa ukuti cili no kutucitikila. Nga cakutila twasumina ukutila Lesa alitutemwa kabili alafwaya ukucita icisuma kuli ifwe tuli no kuleka ukusakamana pa fya kuntanshi. Lyena tuli no kucetekela Lesa ngefyo fye umwana acetekela umufyashi uyo uwakwata ukutemwa. Lyena amafya nefya kulungulusha fyesu fili no kufumishiwapo [ukuluba], pa mulandu wakuti ubufwayo bwesu buli no ku pyanishiwapo no bufwayo bwakwa Lesa.”—Thoughts from the Mount of Blessing, pp. 100, 101.

eng:
4. 	God’s Revelation 	Wed, Sep 2
a. 	Wherein has Christ placed the clearest revelations of God’s plan for the salvation of men? John 5:39; Isaiah 34:16.
“God speaks to us in His word. Here we have in clearer lines the revelation of His character, of His dealings with men, and the great work of redemption.”—Steps to Christ, p. 87.
b. 	What should be done daily by all who desire to grow in the strength and power of God? John 6:53, 63; Colossians 3:1, 2.
“The theme of redemption is one that the angels desire to look into; it will be the science and the song of the redeemed throughout the ceaseless ages of eternity. Is it not worthy of careful thought and study now? The infinite mercy and love of Jesus, the sacrifice made in our behalf, call for the most serious and solemn reflection. We should dwell upon the character of our dear Redeemer and Intercessor. We should meditate upon the mission of Him who came to save His people from their sins.”—Ibid., pp. 88, 89.
c. 	How are we to take God’s word into our hearts? Matthew 4:4; 2 Timothy 2:15.
“No one with a spirit to appreciate its teaching can read a single passage from the Bible without gaining from it some helpful thought. But the most valuable teaching of the Bible is not to be gained by occasional or disconnected study. Its great system of truth is not so presented as to be discerned by the hasty or careless reader. Many of its treasures lie far beneath the surface, and can be obtained only by diligent research and continuous effort. The truths that go to make up the great whole must be searched out and gathered up, ‘here a little, and there a little.’ Isaiah 28:10.
“When thus searched out and brought together, they will be found to be perfectly fitted to one another. Each Gospel is a supplement to the others, every prophecy an explanation of another, every truth a development of some other truth. The types of the Jewish economy are made plain by the gospel. Every principle in the word of God has its place, every fact its bearing. And the complete structure, in design and execution, bears testimony to its Author. Such a structure no mind but that of the Infinite could conceive or fashion.”—Education, pp. 123, 124.
bem:
4. 	UKUSOKOLOLA KWAKWA LESA  	Cine, Ulusuba lunono 2
a. 	Ni muli cinshi umo Klistu abika ukusokolola ukwa tambalala ukwa bwanshiko bwakwa Lesa pa lwepusukilo lya Bantu? Yohane 5:39; Esaya 34:16.
“Lesa alanda kuli ifwe mu mashiwi yakwe. Umubele wakwe walisokololwa mu musango uwa tambalala, ukubomba kwakwe na bantu, kabili no mulimo uu kalamba uwe pususkilo.”—Steps to Christ, p. 87.
b. 	Bushe finshi fifwile ukucitika cila bushiku kuli abo bonse abakabila ukukula mu bukose na maka yakwa Lesa? Yohane 6:53, 63; Kolose 3:1, 2.
“Umutande we pusukilo caliba cintu cimo ico abangeli bakabila ukulolekeshamo; cikaba lisambililo kabili ulwimbo lya balubulwa munkulo fye shonse isha muyayaya. Bushe tacilingile ukucitonkanyapo kabili ukusambililapo mukubikako amano? Uluse ulushipwa elyo no kutemwa kwakwa Yesu, ilambo ilyapelwe mu cifulo cesu, citweba ukuposeshako amano kabili ukutontonkanyapo mukushika. Tufwile ukutontonkanyapo pa mubele wakwa kalubula wesu kabili kapapatila. Tufwile ukwetetula pa mulimo wakwe uyo uwaishile mukupususha abantu bakwe ukufuma kulubembu lwabo.”—Ibid., pp. 88, 89.
c. 	Bushe tufwile ukubika shani amashiwi yakwa Lesa mu mitima yesu? Mateo 4:4; 2 Timote 2:15.
“Takwaba nangu umo uwakwata umupashi wakutasha isambilisho lya cipingo uwingabelengamo amashiwi ukwabula ukunonkamo ukwafwilishiwa mu malangulushi.  Lelo isambilisho ilikankala tekuti linonkwe fye ukupitila mukusambilila fye limo-limo nangula ukwabula mukutwalilila.  Umusango calembelwamo icine ca ciko [icipingo] tawaba wa kwilukwa kuli kabelenga uwaba mu musango wa kupamfiwa kabili uu shaposako na mano. Icuma caciko icingi tacaba pa mbili-mbili, kabili kuti canonkwa fye ukupitila mu kufwailisha mukushika kabili na mukutwalilila mumaka. Icine ico icipanga icituntulu icikulu cifwile ca sangwa kabili no kucibika pamo, ‘utunono apa, kabili natumbi palya.’Esaya 28:10.
“Eico ilyo wafwaya kabili no kucileta pamo, fikasangwa ukuba ifya suntinkana kuli cimo ne cinankwe. Cila mbila nsuma ikaba yakulundako kuli imbi, cila busesemo bulondolola ubusesemo bumbi, icine conse cileta icine cimbi. Imitundu ya bwikashi bwabena Yuda bwalilondololwa mu kutambalala. Cila cipope mwishiwi lyakwa Lesa calikwata incende, kabili ne cishinka conse umusango waciko. Kabili umusango calembelwamo, ifyo cayanshikwa cipela ubunte ku wa cilembele. Ubwanshinko ubwakuti ni uyo fye uwa mano aya shipwa e wingacishiba fye nangula ukucipanga.”—Education, pp. 123, 124.

eng:
5. 	Bible Study 	Thu, Sep 3
a. 	What brought comfort and help to Jeremiah in his tumultuous time? Jeremiah 15:16.
“There is nothing more calculated to strengthen the intellect than the study of the Scriptures. No other book is so potent to elevate the thoughts, to give vigor to the faculties, as the broad, ennobling truths of the Bible. If God’s word were studied as it should be, men would have a breadth of mind, a nobility of character, and a stability of purpose rarely seen in these times.”—Steps to Christ, p. 90.
“He who gives the Scriptures close, prayerful attention will gain clear comprehension and sound judgment, as if in turning to God he had reached a higher grade of intelligence.”—Mind, Character, and Personality, vol. 1, p. 95.
b. 	How should the Scriptures be studied and what must precede such Bible study? Psalm 119:9, 11, 16.
“The truth of God, like gold, is not always lying right on the surface; it is to be obtained only by earnest thought and study.”—Gospel Workers, p. 76.
“As the miner discovers veins of precious metal concealed beneath the surface of the earth, so will he who perseveringly searches the word of God as for hid treasure find truths of the greatest value, which are concealed from the view of the careless seeker. The words of inspiration, pondered in the heart, will be as streams flowing from the fountain of life.
“Never should the Bible be studied without prayer. Before opening its pages we should ask for the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit, and it will be given. . . . Angels from the world of light will be with those who in humility of heart seek for divine guidance.”—Steps to Christ, p. 91.
bem:
5. 	UKUSAMBILILA ICIPINGO	Cisano, Sept. 3
a. 	Cinshi caletele ukutalalikwa kabili no bwafwilisho kuli Yeremia munshita yakwe iya bwafya? Yeremiah 15:16.
“Takwaba icalingwa icinga kosha amalangulushi ukucila pa kusambilila amalembo. Takwaba icitabo icakwatisha amaka ku kusumbula amalangulushi, kukupela amaka kubongo, nge cine ca mucipingo icafunguluka icipela amano. Ngacakuti ishiwi lyakwa Lesa lyalesambililwa ngefyo cifwile ukuba, abantu nga balikwata amano aya funguluka, kabili na bumpomfu bwa mubele, kabili no kushikatala kwa bufwayo uko ukushaseka munshita shino.”—Steps to Christ, p. 90.
“Uyo uu poseshako amano ku malembo mukupepa akanonka imyumfwile iya tambalala kabili no bupingushi ubusuma, pa kupilibukila kuli Lesa alikwata ukufika pa mano aya sumbuka.”—Mind, Character, and Personality, vol. 1, p. 95.
b. 	Bushe amalembo yafwile ya sambililwa shani kabili cinshi cifwile ukutangilila ukusambilila kwa cipingo? Malumbo 119:9, 11, 16.
“Icine cakwa Lesa, nga golide uwakosa, te lyonse cibafye pa bwelu; kuti canonkwa fye ukupitila mu kutontonkanya mukushinka kabili na mu kusambilila.”—Gospel Workers, p. 76.
“Ngefyo fye shi mikoti asanga utupandwa twamabwe ayauma umutengo utwafiswa pashi ya mushili wa calo, efyo cikaba nakuli uyo uu fwailisha mukushipikisha mufyalembwa ifye shiwi lyakwa Lesa nge fikwatwa ifya fiswa akasanga icine icamutengo ukalamba, ico icafiswa  ku menso yakwe uyo uu cifwaya ukwabula ukuposako amano. Amashiwa aya putwamo [aya mushilo], ngayatontonkani shiwapo mu mutima, yakaba ngo tumana utufuma ku kamfuku-mfuku ka mweo.
“Icipingo tacifwile ukusambililwa ukwabula ipepo. Ilyo tatulaba ukupukula ama pepala yaciko tufwile ukulomba umupashi wa mukushilo ukutusanikila, kabili ici cili no kupelwa. . . . Abangeli ukufuma ku calo ca lubuto bali no kuba nabo ukupitila mukuicefye kwa balefwaya ukutungululwa na BuLesa.”—Steps to Christ, p. 91.

eng:
Personal Review Questions 	Fri, Sep 4
1. 	What teaching method was used by our Saviour to reach the people?
2. 	What provision has God made to reveal Himself to all—including those who have no access to His Word?
3. 	What may be learned through the providences of God?
4. 	Describe the attitude we are to have toward the Bible as the revelation of God.
5. 	What experience of Jeremiah with reference to the scriptures should be repeated?
bem:
AMEPUSHO YA KUYASUKILA CILA UMO	Ubwa Mutanda, Sep 4
1. 	Misambilishishe nshi iyo iya lebomfeshiwa na kapususha wesu mu kufunda abantu?
2. 	Chintu nshi ico Lesa abikako mu kuisokolola umwine kuli bonse— ukulundapo fye na kuli abo aba shingakwata ishuko ku cebo cakwe?
3. 	Finshi finga sambililwamo mu fya kuteyanya kwakwe fye Lesa?
4. 	Londolola umubelo tufwile ukukwata ku cipingo ico caba ngo busokololo bwakwa Lesa
5. 	Cibelesho nshi icakwa Yeremia pa cikumine ifyalembwa ico cifwile caba ica kubwekeshiwapo?

eng:
1. 	The Great Suppliant 	Sun, Sep 6
a. 	As the Son of man, what did Jesus find necessary? Luke 5:16; Mark 6:46.
“Behold the Son of God bowed in prayer to His Father! Though He is the Son of God, He strengthens His faith by prayer, and by communion with Heaven gathers to Himself power to resist evil and to minister to the needs of men. As the Elder Brother of our race, He knows the necessities of those who, compassed with infirmity and living in a world of sin and temptation, still desire to serve Him. He knows that the messengers whom He sees fit to send are weak, erring men; but to all who give themselves wholly to His service He promises divine aid. His own example is an assurance that earnest, persevering supplication to God in faith—faith that leads to entire dependence upon God, and unreserved consecration to His work—will avail to bring to men the Holy Spirit’s aid in the battle against sin.”—Gospel Workers, p. 511.
b. 	How is Christ’s practice of prayer an example for us? Mark 1:35; Luke 6:12.
“Jesus Himself, while He dwelt among men, was often in prayer.”—Steps to Christ, p. 93.
bem:
1. 	KAPAPATILA MUKALAMBA 	Cimo, Sep 6
a. 	Ngo mwana wa Muntu, Bushe Finshi Yesu asangile ukuba ifya fwaikwa? Luka 5:16; Marko 6:46.
“ Moneni umwana wakwa Lesa ali icefeshe Kuli wishi mukupepa!  Nangula aba mwana wakwa Lesa, akosha icitetekelo cakwe ukupitila mukupepa, kabili mukulanshanya no mulu alakwata amaka ayakukanya ulubembu kabili no kubombela pa kukabila Kwa bantu. Nga munyina wabo mukalamba uwa mutundu wa buntu, alishiba ifya kukabila kwabo, aba shingulukwa no bunake kabili abekala mu calo ca lubembu elyo na matunko, abacili bafwaisha ukumubombela.  Alishiba ukuti intumi isho amona ukuba ishalinga ukutuma shabunake, bantu abafilubo; lelo abo abaipela umupwilapo ku mulimo wakwe alibalaya ubwafwilisho bwa buLesa. Icakumwenako cakwe umwine caliba bulayo ubwakuti, ukupapata mucishinka, mukutwalilila kabili mucitetekelo Kuli Lesa—icitetekelo icitwala mukushintila umupwilapo pali Lesa, kabili no kuipela onse ku mulimo wakwe—fikaleta ishuko lya kwafwiwa na mupashi wa Mushilo ku bantu mukushashala kwabo no lubembu.”—Gospel Workers, p. 511.
b. 	Bushe ipepo lyakwa Klistu lyaba shani cakumwenako kuli baifwe? Marko 1:35; Luka 6:12.
“Yesu umwine, ilyo aikele pakati kabantu, alepepa lyonse.”—Steps to Christ, p. 93.

eng:
2. 	Christ’s Prayer 	Mon, Sep 7
a. 	How did Jesus teach His disciples to pray? Luke 11:1–4.
“When Jesus was upon the earth, He taught His disciples how to pray. He directed them to present their daily needs before God, and to cast all their care upon Him. And the assurance He gave them that their petitions should be heard, is assurance also to us. . . .
“He is a brother in our infirmities, ‘in all points tempted like as we are;’ but as the sinless one His nature recoiled from evil; He endured struggles and torture of soul in a world of sin. His humanity made prayer a necessity and a privilege. He found comfort and joy in communion with His Father. And if the Saviour of men, the Son of God, felt the need of prayer, how much more should feeble, sinful mortals feel the necessity of fervent, constant prayer.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 93, 94.
b. 	How does the Bible describe Christ’s devotion, and the reason this was so important? Isaiah 50:4; Hebrews 2:10; 5:7–9.
“As the human was upon Him, He felt His need of strength from His Father. He had select places of prayer. He loved to hold communion with His Father in the solitude of the mountain. In this exercise His holy, human soul was strengthened for the duties and trials of the day. Our Saviour identifies Himself with our needs and weaknesses, in that He became a suppliant, a nightly petitioner, seeking from His Father fresh supplies of strength, to come forth invigorated and refreshed, braced for duty and trial. He is our example in all things.”—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 2, pp. 201, 202.
“I saw that there is not one in twenty of the youth who knows what experimental religion is. They serve themselves and yet profess to be servants of Christ; but unless the spell which is upon them be broken, they will soon realize that the portion of the transgressor is theirs. As for self-denial or sacrifice for the truth’s sake, they have found an easier way above it all. As for the earnest pleading with tears and strong cries to God for His pardoning grace and for strength from Him to resist the temptations of Satan, they have found it unnecessary to be so earnest and zealous; they can get along well without it. Christ, the King of glory, went often alone to the mountains and desert places to pour out His soul’s request to His Father; but sinful man, in whom is no strength, thinks he can live without so much prayer.”—Ibid., vol. 1, pp. 504, 505.
bem:
2. 	IPEPO LYAKWA KLISTU	Cibili, ulusuba lunono 7
a. 	Bushe Yesu afundishe shani abasambi bakwe ukupepa? Luka 11:1–4.
“Ilyo Yesu ali pa calo, alisambilishe abasambi bakwe ifya kupepa. Abasontelele ukutwala ifyakukabila fyabo ifyacila bushiku kuntanshi yakwa Lesa, kabili no kubika ifya kusakamana fyabo fyonse pali wena.  Kabili no bulayo abapele bwa kuti ukupapata kwabo ku kumfwika, abulayo bumo bwine ubwapelwa nakuli baifwe.
“Ni munyinefwe mu fyakuculusha kwesu, ‘alitunkilwe muli fyonse ngefyo fye tutunkwa; ‘lelo ngo wabula ulubembu umubele wakwe watalwike kububi; ashipikishe kulungulushiwa elyo na kushashala kwa mupashi mu calo ca lubembu.  Ukuinasha kwakwe kwalengele ipepo ukuba ica fwaikwa kabili ishuko. Asangile ukutalalikwa elyo ne nsansa mukulanshanya na wishi. Kabili nga cakuti umupusushi wa bantu, umwana wakwa Lesa aumfwile ubukabilo bwe pepo, na kucilishamo ifibumbwa ifyanaka kabili ifya lubembu fifwile fyakabilisha ipepo ilyashika kabili ilya mukutwalilila.”—Steps to Christ, pp. 93, 94.
b. 	Bushe icipingo cilondolola shani imipepele yakwa Klistu, kabili cinshi ici cabelele icikankala? Esaya 50:4; Aba Hebele 2:10; 5:7–9.
“Nge fyo bumuntu bwali pali wena, alekabila ubukose ukufuma kuli wishi. Alisalise incede ukwa kupepela. Alitemenwe ukulanshanya na wishi eka kulumpili. Mukucita ifi umupashi wakwe walikoshiwe kukubomba imilimo kabili na kumatunko ya cilabushiku. Kapususha wesu ali kwetefye ukukabila kumo kwine kabili na mabunake ngaifwe, ukupitila muli ifi aishile ba kapapatila, kapepa wa munshita ya bushiku, ukulomba kuli wishi amaka ayapya, pakuti engesa mumaka kabili uwakoshiwa, uwaipekanya kumilimo kabili naku mesho. Aliba cakumwenako cesu mufintu fyonse.”—Testimonies for the Church, vol. 2, pp. 201, 202.
“Nalimwene ukuti tapali umupungwe nangu umo pa bapungwe amakumi yabili uwaishiba ifyo bukapepa bwa muficitwa bupilibula. Balaitumikila [ukuibombela] abene elyo panshita imo ine baleitunga ukuba ababomfi bakwa Klistu; nomba kanofye nga cakutila ububi [icitipu] ubwabikwa pali bena bwaonaulwa, nga teifyo bali no kukutuka nomba line fye ukutila icakaniko cabikilwa katoba wefunde nabo bene cabo [na cibakuma]. Pa cikumine ukuikanya nangula ukuipela bulilambo pa mulandu wacine, balisangapo icintu icayangu ukucila pali ico. Pacikumine ukupapata mucishinka kabili mufilamba no kulila mukukosa kuli Lesa ukulomba icikuku cakwelela kabili na maka ukufuma kuli wena kukucimfya amatunko yakwa Shatani, tabacimonamo ici ukuba icafwaikwa mukuba aba posako amano kabili na mukuba abapimpa; kuti baikala fye bwino bena ukwabula ifi fintu.   Klistu, imfumu yalulumbi, aleya ilingi eka muncende sha mpili na mufiswebebe mu kulomba kuli wishi ifyo umutima wakwe walekabila; lelo umuntu uwalubembu, uwabula na maka, atontonkanya ukuti ena kuti aikala ukwabula ukupepa sana.”—Ibid., vol. 1, pp. 504, 505.

eng:
3. 	The Privilege of Prayer 	Tue, Sep 8
a. 	How did Jesus reveal to us the attitude of His Father toward human need? Matthew 6:6; 7:7–11.
“Our heavenly Father waits to bestow upon us the fullness of His blessing. It is our privilege to drink largely at the fountain of boundless love. What a wonder it is that we pray so little! God is ready and willing to hear the sincere prayer of the humblest of His children, and yet there is much manifest reluctance on our part to make known our wants to God.”—Steps to Christ, p. 94.
“God is too wise to err, and too good to withhold any good thing from them that walk uprightly. Then do not fear to trust Him, even though you do not see the immediate answer to your prayers. Rely upon His sure promise, ‘Ask, and it shall be given you.’ ”—Ibid., p. 96.
b. 	What prevents our petitions from being heard by the Lord? Psalm 66:18; Proverbs 28:13.
“Our minds may be drawn out toward [God]; we may meditate upon His works, His mercies, His blessings; but this is not, in the fullest sense, communing with Him. In order to commune with God, we must have something to say to Him concerning our actual life.”—Ibid., p. 93.
“What can the angels of heaven think of poor helpless human beings, who are subject to temptation, when God’s heart of infinite love yearns toward them, ready to give them more than they can ask or think, and yet they pray so little and have so little faith? The angels love to bow before God, they love to be near Him. They regard communion with God as their highest joy; and yet the children of earth, who need so much the help that God only can give, seem satisfied to walk without the light of His Spirit, the companionship of His presence.
“The darkness of the evil one encloses those who neglect to pray. The whispered temptations of the enemy entice them to sin; and it is all because they do not make use of the privileges that God has given them in the divine appointment of prayer.”—Ibid., p. 94.
“If we regard iniquity in our hearts, if we cling to any known sin, the Lord will not hear us; but the prayer of the penitent, contrite soul is always accepted. When all known wrongs are righted, we may believe that God will answer our petitions. Our own merit will never commend us to the favor of God; it is the worthiness of Jesus that will save us, His blood that will cleanse us; yet we have a work to do in complying with the conditions of acceptance.”—Ibid., p. 95.
bem:
3. 	UBUKANKALA BWE PEPO 	Citatu, Ulusuba lunono 8
a. 	Bushe Yesu asokolwelwe shani umubela wakwa wishi kukukabila kwa bantu? Mateo 6:6; 7:7–11.
“Shifwe wa mumulu alolela ukubika pali ifwe umwisulo uwe palo lyakwe. Lishuko lyesu ukunwa apakalamba kukamfuku-mfuku kakutemwa ukushifilwa. Iyee ifyo caba ica kupapusha icakuti tupepa fye panono! Lesa alifye uwaiteyanya kabili uwafwaisha ukukutika ipepo lya cishinka ilya mwana uyo uwainasha sana pa bana bakwe, lelo kwaliba uku shingashinga kulubali lwesu mukulenga ifyakukabila fyesu fishibwe kuli Lesa.”—Steps to Christ, p. 94.
“Lesa alikwatisha amano uwa kuti alube, kabili musuma sana uwakuti teti akane ukupela icintu conse icisuma kuli bena abenda mu bulungami. Mwilatina ukumucetekela ena, nangula amapepo yenu tayaswikwe palya pene. Shintilileni pa bulayo bwakwe ubwa cishinka, ‘Lombeni, kabili cikapelwa kuli imwe.’ ”—Ibid., p. 96.
b. 	Finshi ficingilisha ukupapata kwesu ukumfwika kuli shikulu? Malumbo 66:18; Mapinda 28:13.
“Amano yesu kuti ya palamikwa kuli [Lesa]; Kuti twalangulukapo na pa mashiwi yakwe, pa luse lwakwe, pa mapalo yakwe; lelo ifi temukufikapo kwa mano yonse, mukusosa nankwe. Pakuti twingalanshanya na Lesa, tufwile ukukwata fimo ifya kumweba pa cikumine umweo wesu.”—Ibid., p. 93.
“Bushe finshi abangeli bengatontonkanya pa bantu nse, abo abasangwa mu matunko, ilyo ninshi umutima wakwa Lesa uwa kutemwa ulekubila  bena, uwaipekanisha ukubapela ifyacila pafyo bengalomba nangula pafyo batontonkanya, nomba bapepafye panono sana kabili bakwata icitetekelo icinono sana? Abangeli balitemwa ukuicefya kuntashi yakwa Lesa, balitemwa ukuba mupepi nankwe. Babika ukulanshanya nankwe ngensansa shabo ishacila; lelo abana aba pesonde, abakabila ubwafwilisho ubo Lesa e kafye engapela, balamoneka ukuba abaikushiwa ukwenda ukwabula ulubuto lwa mupashi wakwe, cibusa wa kubapo kwakwe.
“Imfifi ya mubifi ishinguluka abo bonse abalekelesha ukupepa. Ukutotosha kwa matunko ya mulwani kubalosha kukubembuka; kabili ni pamulandu wakuti tababonfya ishuko ilyo Lesa abapela mwipepo lyabu Lesa.”—Ibid., p. 94.
“Ngacakuti twasunga ububifi mu mitima yesu, ngacakuti twalambatila kulubembu ululi lonse ulwaishibikwa, Shikulu takatumfwe; lelo ipepo lya mutima wa mupashi uwa funshika, uwalapila lilapokelelwa lyonse. Ilyo ifilubo fyonse fyalungikwa, kuti twacetekela ukuti Lesa akasuka ukulomba kwesu. Ubusuma bwesu tabwa katuwaminishe kuli Lesa; lelo bukankala bwakwa Yesu e bukatupususha ifwe, umulopa wakwe ukatusamba ifwe; lelo natukwata umulimo wesu uwa kunakila ku filefwaikwa pakuti tupokelelwe.”—Ibid., p. 95.

eng:
4. 	Prevailing Prayer 	Wed, Sep 9
a. 	What are the important elements of prevailing prayer in contrast with weak and ineffective prayer? Hebrews 11:6; Mark 11:24.
“When we do not receive the very things we asked for, at the time we ask, we are still to believe that the Lord hears and that He will answer our prayers. We are so erring and shortsighted that we sometimes ask for things that would not be a blessing to us, and our heavenly Father in love answers our prayers by giving us that which will be for our highest good—that which we ourselves would desire if with vision divinely enlightened we could see all things as they really are. When our prayers seem not to be answered, we are to cling to the promise; for the time of answering will surely come, and we shall receive the blessing we need most.”—Steps to Christ, p. 96.
b. 	In order for prayer to be heard by the Lord, what spirit must we have? Matthew 6:12; Mark 11:25, 26.
“When we come to ask mercy and blessing from God we should have a spirit of love and forgiveness in our own hearts. How can we pray, ‘Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors,’ and yet indulge an unforgiving spirit? Matthew 6:12. If we expect our own prayers to be heard we must forgive others in the same manner and to the same extent as we hope to be forgiven.”—Ibid., p. 97. [Author’s italics.]
c. 	What can we learn from Elijah’s prayer for rain? 1 Kings 18:41–45.
“The servant watched while Elijah prayed. Six times he returned from the watch, saying, There is nothing, no cloud, no sign of rain. But the prophet did not give up in discouragement. He kept reviewing his life, to see where he had failed to honor God, he confessed his sins, and thus continued to afflict his soul before God, while watching for a token that his prayer was answered. As he searched his heart, he seemed to be less and less, both in his own estimation and in the sight of God. It seemed to him that he was nothing, and that God was everything; and when he reached the point of renouncing self, while he clung to the Saviour as his only strength and righteousness, the answer came.”—The SDA Bible Commentary, vol. 2, p. 1035.
bem:
4. 	IPEPO LYA KUCINFYA 	Cine, Ulusuba lunono 9
a. 	Bukankala nshi bwaba mwipepo ilya kucinfya ku kupusanako ne pepo ili shafikapo kabili ilya bunake? BaHebele 11:6; Marko 11:24.
“Ilyo tatupokelele ifintu ifyo fine twalombele, panshita twalomba, tufwile ukucetekela uktila Shikulu alomfwa kabili akasuka amapepo yesu. Twaliba mukuluba kabili abamonafye mupepi icakuti limo tulomba ifintu ifintu ifishingaba lipalo kuli ifwe, kabili shifwe wa mu mulu mukutemwa alasuka amapeo yesu ukupitila mukutupela ico icingaba icawamisha kuli fiwe—ico eco fwebene twinga kabilla nga cakuti twamwene ifintu ifyo fyaba nga cakuti twashibwilwe ne mimwene ya buLesa. Ilyo amapepo yesu yamoneka ukukana yasukwa, tufwile ukulambatila kubulayo; pantu inshita yakwasukwa mucine fye ikesa, kabili tukapokelela ipalo tukabilisha.”—Steps to Christ, p. 96.
b. 	Pakutila ipepo lyesu lingasukwa na Shikulu, Mupashi nshi tufwile ukukwata? Mateo 6:12; Marko 11:25, 26.
“Ilyo twaisa mukulomba uluse kabili ne palo ukufuma kuli Lesa tufwile ukukwata umupashi wakutemwa kabili no kwelela mu mitima yesu. Bushe kuti twapepa shani ati, ‘tubeleleni uluse’, ngefyo twelela abatubifya,’ elyo ninshi tatwa kwata umupashi wakwelela? Mateo 6:12. Nga cakuti tulefwaya amapepo yesu ukumfwika tufwile ukwelela bambi mumusango umowine kabili na ku mushinku umowine ngefyo tusubila ukwelelwa.”—Ibid., p. 97. [Author’s italics.]
c. 	Cinshi twingasambililako kwipepo lya kwa Eliya ilyakupepela imfula? 1 Ishamfumu 18:41–45.
“Umubomfi aletamba Eliya ilyo alepepa. Pa miku mutanda alibwelele mukuloleshako, atile, takuli nangu cimo, takuli ikumbi, takuli icilangililo ca mfula. Lelo kasesema tanashiwe no kuleka. Akonkenyepo fye ukuceceta umweo wakwe, ukumona apo afililwe ukucindika Lesa, ali yebelele imembu shakwe, kabili eico atwalilile ukulungulusha umupashi wakwe kuntashi yakwa Lesa, ilyo atwalilile ukulolesha ku cakulangisha ukuti ipepo lyakwe lya lyaswikwe.  Ilyo alececeta umutima wakwe, amoneke ukuba uwakucepelako, mukuilinga kwakwe umwine elyo fye na kucinso cakwa Lesa. Camoneke kuli wena ukuti tapali ifyo ali, kabili Lesa ewali fyonse; kabili ilyo afikile pa mushinku wakuisusha umwine, ilyo acili na lambatila ku mupusushi ngo wakumukosha ekafye kabili ubololoke, ubwasuko bwalishile.”—The SDA Bible Commentary, vol. 2, p. 1035.

eng:
5. 	Perseverance in Prayer 	Thu, Sep 10
a. 	What important counsel do the apostles give concerning prayer? 1 Peter 4:7; Philippians 4:6.
“There is a necessity for diligence in prayer; let nothing hinder you. Make every effort to keep open the communion between Jesus and your own soul. Seek every opportunity to go where prayer is wont to be made. Those who are really seeking for communion with God will be seen in the prayer meeting, faithful to do their duty and earnest and anxious to reap all the benefits they can gain. They will improve every opportunity of placing themselves where they can receive the rays of light from heaven.”—Steps to Christ, p. 98.
b. 	Like any parent, what does the Lord expect His children to do? Luke 11:10, 13; John 14:13, 14.
“ ‘In My name,’ Christ bade His disciples pray. In Christ’s name His followers are to stand before God. Through the value of the sacrifice made for them, they are of value in the Lord’s sight. Because of the imputed righteousness of Christ they are accounted precious. For Christ’s sake the Lord pardons those that fear Him. He does not see in them the vileness of the sinner. He recognizes in them the likeness of His Son, in whom they believe.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 667.
“There is no time or place in which it is inappropriate to offer up a petition to God. There is nothing that can prevent us from lifting up our hearts in the spirit of earnest prayer. In the crowds of the street, in the midst of a business engagement, we may send up a petition to God and plead for divine guidance, as did Nehemiah when he made his request before King Artaxerxes. A closet of communion may be found wherever we are.”—Steps to Christ, p. 99.
bem:
5. 	UKUSHIPIKISHA MUKUPEPA 	Cisano, ulusuba lunono 10
a. 	Nibumpanda mano nshi ubukankala ubo abasole bapela pa cikumine ipepo? 1 Petelo 4:7; Filipe 4:6.
"Caliba icafwaikwa ukuposeshako amano mwipepo; mwileka nangu fye cimo cimuicikilishe. Esheni na maka yonse ukwisula ukulanshanya pakati kakwa Yesu no mupashi wenu mwebene. Bonfyeni ishuko lyonse ukuya uko ipepo lifwile ukupepwa. Abo bonse abalefwaya ukulanshanya na Lesa mu cishinka bali no kusangwa mu kulongana kwa mapepo, ukuba abacishinka mukubomba umulimo wabo kabili abacishinka kabili abafwaisha ifinonsho ifyo benga kwata. Bakabonfya ishuko lyonse ukuibika mucifulo abane umo bengakwata ukupokelela imyengelele ya lubuto ukufuma ku mulu.”—Steps to Christ, p. 98.
b. 	Ngefyo fye caba kumufyashi onse, bushe finshi Shikulu asubila ifwe ukucita? Luka 11:10, 13; Yohane 14:13, 14.
“ ‘Mwishina lyandi emo mulepepela,” efyo Klistu akambishe abasambi bakwe. Mwishina lyakwa Klistu emo bakakonka bakwe bali no kwimininina kuntanshi yakwa Lesa. Ukupitila mu mutengo welambo alipile pa mulandu wabo, baliba aba mutengo ku menso yakwe. Pa mulandu wabololoke ubwapelwa ubwakwa Klistu balapendwa ukuba aba mutengo wa pamulu. Pamulandu wakwa Klistu Shikulu alelela bonse abamutina. Tamona muli bena ukubipa kwa mubembu. Amonamo mulibena ukupalana no mwana wakwe, muli uyo basuminamo.”—The Desire of Ages, p. 667.
“Takwaba inshita nangu incende iishaba iyalinga ukupepa kuli Lesa. Takwaba nangu cimo icinga tukanya ukusumbula imitima yesu mu mupashi we pepo ilya cishinka. Mwibumba lya mu misebo, ilyo tulecita amakwebo, kuti twalomba kuli Lesa kabili no kupapatila ukutungululwa kwa buLesa, ngefya citile Nemiya ilyo alombele kuntanshi ya mfumu Artaxerxes. Incende ya kulanshanishishapo kuti yasangwa konse uko twingasangwa.”—Steps to Christ, p. 99.

eng:
1. 	What is Doubt? 	Sun, Sep 13
a. 	What should we remember when tempted to vacillate between faith and doubt? James 1:5–7.
“[The Saviour’s] promise is only to those who are willing to follow the Lord wholly. God does not force the will of any; hence He cannot lead those who are too proud to be taught, who are bent upon having their own way. Of the double-minded man—he who seeks to follow his own will, while professing to do the will of God—it is written, ‘Let not that man think that he shall receive anything of the Lord.’ James 1:7.”—Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 384.
b. 	What has the Lord given in order to overcome doubt? Psalm 119:105; Hebrews 11:1, 3, 6.
“Our faith must rest upon evidence, not demonstration. Those who wish to doubt will have opportunity; while those who really desire to know the truth will find plenty of evidence on which to rest their faith.”—Steps to Christ, p. 105.
“God has given in His word sufficient evidence of its divine character. The great truths which concern our redemption are clearly presented. By the aid of the Holy Spirit, which is promised to all who seek it in sincerity, every man may understand these truths for himself. God has granted to men a strong foundation upon which to rest their faith.”—The Great Controversy, pp. 526, 527.
bem:
1. 	BUSHE UKUTWISHIKA CHINSHI? 	Cimo, Sept 13
a. 	Bushe chinshi ico tufwile ukula ibukisha ilintu twa tunkilwa kuku lesha-lesha pakati kakucetekela nokutwishika? Yakobo 1:5–7.
“Ubulayo bwa Mupusuhi bwabafye kuli abo abalefwaisha ukukonka shikulu mu mupwilapo. Lesa tapatikisha ubufwayo bwa muntu nangu umo; eico teti atungulule abo abakwatisha icilumba icakufundwa, abo abakoselela fye ukucita ifyo balefwaya abene. Palwa muntu uyo untu amalangulushi yakwe tayaba pa cintu cimo, uyo uufwaya ukukonka ubufwayo bwakwe umwine, na pa nshita imoine aleitunga ukucita ubufwayo bwakwa Lesa, calilembwa ukuti, ‘Uyo umuntu etontonkanya ukuti ali no kupokelela icili conse ukufuma kuli Lesa.’ Yakobo 1:7.”—Patriarchs and Prophets, p. 384.
b. 	Fintunshi Shikulu apela ifyo twinga bomfya mukucimfya ukutwishika? Amalumbo 119:105; Abahebele 11:1, 3, 6.
“Icicetekelo cesu cifwile cashintilila pa fishinikisho, tepafilangililo nakalya. Abo aba fwaya ukutwishika bali nokusanga umwakutwishikila; elyo abo aba fwaya mucishinka ukwishiba icine bali nokusanga ifishininkisho ifingi ifyo benga shintililapo icicetekelo cabo.”—Steps to Christ, p. 105.
“Lesa mwishiwi lyakwe alipela ifishininkisho ifya kumanina pa lwa bumushilo buntu lyakwata. Ifishinka ifikalamba ifya kuma ukulubulwa kwesu fyalipelwa muku tambalala. Uku pitila mu bwafilisho bwa mupashi wamushilo, uyo untu walaiwa kuli bonse abaufwaya muli bucishinka, umuntu onse kuti akwata ukumfwikisha ifishinka ifi palwakwe. Lesa ali pela ku bantu umufula uwakosa uyo untu benga shitililapo icicetekelo cabo.”—The Great Controversy, pp. 526, 527.

eng:
2. 	Divine Mysteries 	Mon, Sep 14
a. 	How should we relate to mysteries which God has not explained? Deuteronomy 29:29; Job 38:4–11.
“The word of God, like the character of its divine Author, presents mysteries that can never be fully comprehended by finite beings. The entrance of sin into the world, the incarnation of Christ, regeneration, the resurrection, and many other subjects presented in the Bible, are mysteries too deep for the human mind to explain, or even fully to comprehend. But we have no reason to doubt God’s word because we cannot understand the mysteries of His providence.”—Steps to Christ, p. 106.
“God does not compel men to give up their unbelief. Before them are light and darkness, truth and error. It is for them to decide which they will accept. The human mind is endowed with power to discriminate between right and wrong. God designs that men shall not decide from impulse, but from weight of evidence, carefully comparing scripture with scripture. Had the Jews laid by their prejudice and compared written prophecy with the facts characterizing the life of Jesus, they would have perceived a beautiful harmony between the prophecies and their fulfillment in the life and ministry of the lowly Galilean.
“Many are deceived today in the same way as were the Jews. Religious teachers read the Bible in the light of their own understanding and traditions; and the people do not search the Scriptures for themselves, and judge for themselves as to what is truth; but they yield up their judgment, and commit their souls to their leaders. The preaching and teaching of His word is one of the means that God has ordained for diffusing light; but we must bring every man’s teaching to the test of Scripture.”—The Desire of Ages, pp. 458, 459.
b. 	How is it recognized in the Bible that there are things hard to be understood? 2 Peter 3:16.
“The difficulties of Scripture have been urged by skeptics as an argument against the Bible; but so far from this, they constitute a strong evidence of its divine inspiration. If it contained no account of God but that which we could easily comprehend; if His greatness and majesty could be grasped by finite minds, then the Bible would not bear the unmistakable credentials of divine authority. The very grandeur and mystery of the themes presented should inspire faith in it as the word of God.”—Steps to Christ, p. 107.
bem:
2. 	IFYANKAMA IFYASHILA                                                                       Cibili, Sept 14
a. Ni munshila nshi tufwile twasendela ifyankama ifyo fintu Lesa talondolola? Amalango 29:29; Yobo 38:4–11.
"Ishiwi lyakwa Lesa, pamo ngo mubele wakwata kalemba waliko uwa mushilo, lyakwata ifyankama ifishingo mfwikishiwa umupwilapo na bantu abena kufwa. Ukwisa kwa lubembu mwi sonde, uku fyalwa kwa-kwa Klistu, ukupuputulwa, ukubushiwa ukufuma kumfwa, ne milandu imbi iyapelwa mu cipingo, yaba ni nkama isho amano ya muntu teti yakwate ukulondolola, nangu kumfwikisha umupwilapo. Lelo ici tacatupela insambu isha kutwishika ishiwi lyakwa Lesa pa mulandu wakutila teti tumfwikishe inkama sha bwafwilisho no busunge Bwakwe pali ifwe.”—Steps to Christ, p. 106.
“Lesa tapatikisha abantu ukuleka ukukanasumina kwabo.  Kuntanshi yabo kwabikwa ulubuto nemfifi, icishinka nokuluba. Caba kuli bena ukusalapo ico bengasumina. Kampingu ya muntu yalipelwa amaka ayakulekanya pa cintu icibi necisuma. Ubwanshiko bwakwa Lesa bwaba bwakutila umuntu tafwile ukula pangila amabusalo ukupitilafye muku pumikishiwa, lelo kupitila mu mulingo wa fishininkisho, ukupitila mukwampanya ilembo nelembo bwino-bwino. Ababika pa mbali aba Yuda amano yabo abene no kwampanya ubusesemo bwalembelwe kufishinka fyali mu mweo wakwa Yesu, nga balimwene ukwampana ukusuma pakati ka mabusesemo no kufiklishiwa kwa yako mu mweo no butumikishi bwa Uyu umwina Galileya uwali uwa chepesha.
“Abengi na balufiwa ilelo munshila imo ine intu yalubilemo aba Yuda. Ba kafundisha ba fikumine bukapepa bakwata ukubelengela icipingo mu lubuto lwa myumfwile yabo pamo ne ntambi shabo; na bantu nabo tabakwata ukuifwaila mu malembo palwabo, no kuipingwila abene ifishinka; balekela ubupingushi, no kupela imipashi yabo ku ntungulushi shabo. Ukushimikila no kufunda ishiwi Lyakwe yaba e nshila intu Lesa asala ukutila ulubuto lwingaba ulwa kusabankanishiwamo; lelo nangu cingaba ifi tufwile ukwesesha ukufunda kwa muntu onse ukupitila mu malembo.”—The Desire of Ages, pp. 458, 459.
b. 	Bushe cashininkishiwa shani mucipingo ukutila kwaliba ifintu ifyakosa ukumfwikisha? 2 Petelo 3:16.
“Ukukosa kwa malembo kubatwishika kupendwa nga ukuitalika kwa ma lembo ayene yeka aya mu cipingo; lelo ukutali neci, yasangwamo ifishininkisho ifya shika ifya kuba aya kuputwamo na bumushilo. Aciba ukutila tamwali nangu cimo icilanda palwa kwa Lesa lelo mwaisulafye ifyo twingomfwa mukwanguka; aciba ukuti ubukulu Bwakwe no bukata Bwakwe bwali ubwingomfwika ku malangulushi ayakwata impela, icipingo nga tacakwata ifishibilo fya maka ya bumushilo ayo aya shinga twishikwa. Ubucindami bwaciko ne nkama sha fyakwata ukulangishiwamo efifwile ukukosha icicetekelo cesu muli cene ukuba nge ishiwi lyakwa Lesa.”—Steps to hrist, p. 107.

eng:
3. 	Danger of an Unbelieving Heart 	Tue, Sep 15
a. 	What is a particular danger for the believers in these last days? Hebrews 3:12; 2 Timothy 4:3, 4.
“When God sends to men warnings so important that they are represented as proclaimed by holy angels flying in the midst of heaven, He requires every person endowed with reasoning powers to heed the message. The fearful judgments denounced against the worship of the beast and his image (Revelation 14:9–11), should lead all to a diligent study of the prophecies to learn what the mark of the beast is, and how they are to avoid receiving it. But the masses of the people turn away their ears from hearing the truth and are turned unto fables. The apostle Paul declared, looking down to the last days: ‘The time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine.’ 2 Timothy 4:3. That time has fully come. The multitudes do not want Bible truth, because it interferes with the desires of the sinful, world-loving heart; and Satan supplies the deceptions which they love.”—The Great Controversy, pp. 594, 595.
b. 	What is prophesied of the attitude of the two classes in the last days? Daniel 12:10; Revelation 22:11.
“God will have a people upon the earth to maintain the Bible, and the Bible only, as the standard of all doctrines and the basis of all reforms. The opinions of learned men, the deductions of science, the creeds or decisions of ecclesiastical councils, as numerous and discordant as are the churches which they represent, the voice of the majority—not one nor all of these should be regarded as evidence for or against any point of religious faith. Before accepting any doctrine or precept, we should demand a plain ‘Thus said the Lord’ in its support.”—Ibid., p. 595.
“New light will ever be revealed on the word of God to him who is in living connection with the Sun of Righteousness. Let no one come to the conclusion that there is no more truth to be revealed. The diligent, prayerful seeker for truth will find precious rays of light yet to shine forth from the word of God. Many gems are yet scattered that are to be gathered together to become the property of the remnant people of God. But light is not given simply to be a strength to the church, but to be shed upon those who are in darkness.”—Counsels on Sabbath School Work, p. 34.
bem:
3. 	UBUSANSO BWABA MUKUKWATA UMUTIMA UWABULAMO UBUSUMINO 	Citatu, Sept 15
a. 	Cinshi caba ngo busanso ku basumini muli shino inshiku sha kulekelesha? Abahebele 3:12; 2 Timote 4:3, 4.
“Ilyo Lesa atuma amabusoko ku bantu aya kwatisha ubukankala icakuti yalangishiwa nga ayakuba aya landilwe na bamalaika bamushilo abalepupuka mu myulu, Akabila ukutila umuntu onse uyo uwakwata ukushukishiwa na amaka ya kulekanya pafintu enga kwata ukumfwa iyi imbila. Amabupingushi ayo ayakutinya ayakwata ukubikwa pamulandu wakupepa iciswango ne cimpashanya caciko (ubusokololo 14:9–11), yafwile ukutungulula abantu bonse mukusambilila kwama busesemo ukwafikapo mukufwaisha ukwishiba ico ululembo lwa ciswango lupilibula, nefyo bali nokuicingilila ukukana lupokelela. Lelo imintapendwa yabantu yalikana ukumfwa icishinka noku yalwila ku kumfwa imilumbe. Umutumwa Paulo asosele, ukusontelela kunshiku shakulekelesha: ‘Ileisa inshita ilyo tabakafwaye ukukutika kwisambilisho ilituntulu.’ 2 Timote 4:3. Iyi inshita yalifika mukupwililika. Imi ntapendwa ya bantu taifwaya icine ca mucipingo, pa mulandu wakuti cikwata ukupinkana no kufwaya kwa babembu, ukufwaya kwa mutima uwa temwisha icalo; eico ciwa alakwata ukuteyanya ubufi ubo buntu bakwata ukutemwa.”—The Great Controversy, pp. 594, 595.
b. 	Cinshi casesemwa pa mulandu wamubele wa mabumba yabili aya mu nshiku sha kulekelesha? Daniele 12:10; Ubusokololo 22:11.
“Lesa ali nokukwata abantu pa calo abali nokusungilila icipingo, icipingo fye ceka, ukuba ngecipimino ca masambilisho yonse neshintililo lya kufukulula konse. Amalangulushi ya bantu abasambilila , ifyasangwa mumatukuto yabantu, ifipope nangu amabusalo ya filye fya bashimapepo, mubwingi bwafiko nokutalikisha nga fintu ifilonganino fyaimininako fyaba, ishiwi lya cintubwingi— tapafwile ukuba nangu cimo pali ifi icinga pendwa ukuba ngechishinikisho mukwimininako nangu ukutalikisha ifya mu busumino. Ilyo tatulasumina icipope icili conse , tufwile twakwata ukwipusha ngachakutila kuli amashiwi ayalembwa pamulandu wachiko ukufuma kwishiwi lyakwa Lesa  ayatila ‘efyasosa Imfumu’.”—Ibid., p. 595.
“Ulubuto ulupya luli nokutwalilila ukusokololwa peshiwi lyakwa Lesa ku muntu uyo uwakwata ukwikala umweo uwasuntinkana nolubuto lwa bulungami. Umuntu nangu umo etontonkanya ukutila takuli ulubuto nalumbi ululi nokusokololwa. Kafwailisha wa fyachishinka uyo uwaisulamo bukapepa nomukosha, ali nokusanga imyengelele yalubuto iyikankala imbi iyishilati ukubengeshima ukufuma mwishiwi lyakwa Lesa. Kuchiliko amabwe yambi aya uma umutengo ayasalangana ayalingile ukukolonganishiwa pamo nokwisaba ifikwatwa fyabantu bakwa Lesa abashalapo. Ulubuto talupelwafye kuchilonganino ukuba ngamaka kuli cene, lelo kukuba ulwa kubalikila na pabali mu mfifi.”—Counsels on Sabbath School Work, p. 34.

eng:
4. 	The True Cause of Doubt 	Wed, Sep 16
a. 	How can we distinguish between the important and the unimportant? 2 Corinthians 13:5; Titus 3:9–11.
“While God has given ample evidence for faith, He will never remove all excuse for unbelief. All who look for hooks to hang their doubts upon will find them. And those who refuse to accept and obey God’s word until every objection has been removed, and there is no longer an opportunity for doubt, will never come to the light.”—The Great Controversy, p. 527.
b. 	What blessings will come to the humble? James 4:6, 10; 1 Peter 5:6, 7.
“ ‘Every want was supplied, the hunger of my soul was satisfied; and now the Bible is to me the revelation of Jesus Christ. Do you ask why I believe in Jesus? Because He is to me a divine Saviour. Why do I believe the Bible? Because I have found it to be the voice of God to my soul.’ We may have the witness in ourselves that the Bible is true, that Christ is the Son of God. We know that we are not following cunningly devised fables.”—Steps to Christ, p. 112.
c. 	How does the apostle Paul describe the experience of the believer now and in the future? 1 Corinthians 13:12.
“In this life we can only begin to understand the wonderful theme of redemption. With our finite comprehension we may consider most earnestly the shame and the glory, the life and the death, the justice and the mercy, that meet in the cross; yet with the utmost stretch of our mental powers we fail to grasp its full significance. The length and the breadth, the depth and the height, of redeeming love are but dimly comprehended. The plan of redemption will not be fully understood even when the ransomed see as they are seen and know as they are known; but through the eternal ages new truth will continually unfold to the wondering and delighted mind.”—The Great Controversy, p. 651.
“By faith we may look to the hereafter and grasp the pledge of God for a growth of intellect, the human faculties uniting with the divine, and every power of the soul being brought into direct contact with the Source of light. We may rejoice that all which has perplexed us in the providences of God will then be made plain, things hard to be understood will then find an explanation; and where our finite minds discovered only confusion and broken purposes, we shall see the most perfect and beautiful harmony. [1 Corinthians 13:12 quoted.]”—Ibid., pp, 112, 113.
bem:
4. 	ICILENGA UKUTWISHIKA                                                                                       Cine, Sept 16
a. 	Kuti twalekanya shani pa fikwete ubukankala ne fishikwete ? 2 Kolinti 13:5; Tito 3:9–11.
“ Apo Lesa alikwata ukupela ifishininkisho ifya kumanina ifya kukosha icicetekelo, Tali no kufumyapo umwa kulesesha uku kanasumina. Abo bonse abafwaya apa kushintilila ukutwishika kwabo bali no kusanga ifintu bafwaya. Kabili nabo bonse abakana ukusumina no kumfwila ishiwi lyakwa Lesa mukulolela ukuti ifya cilinganya fyonse finga kwata ukufumishiwapo, ukusubila ilyo takushelepo inshila iyili yonse iyakutila benga kwata ukutwishikilamo, tabakatale abesa kulubuto.”—The Great Controversy, p. 527.
b. 	Mapalo nshi yali no kwisa ku baicefya? Yakobo 4:6, 10; 1 Petelo 5:6, 7.
“ ‘Ukufwaya konse kwalipelwe, insala yakwete umupashi wandi yalikushiwe; kabili ne cipingo caba kuli ine ubusokololo bwa-kwa Yesu Klistu. Bushe mulepusha umulandu na suminina muli Yesu? Ni pamulandu wakutila Aba kuli ine Kalubula wamushilo. Bushe cinshi nasuminina icipingo? Ni pamulandu wakuti na cisanga ukuba e shiwi lyakwa Lesa ku mupashi wandi. Kuti twakwata mukati kesu fwebene ubunte ubwakutila icipingo cachishinka, ubunte ubwa kutila Klistu mwana wakwa Lesa. Twalishiba ukuti tatulekonka imilumbe iyo iyapangwa no bucengeshi bwa bantu.”—Steps to Christ, p. 112.
c. 	Bushe umutumwa Paulo alondolola shani icibelesho ca musumini ilelo na munshita ya kuntanshi? 1 kolinto 13:12.
“Muli uno umweo kuti twatendekafye ukumfwa icikope cepusukilo ico icaba icakupapusha. No kumfwikisha kwesu uko ukwaba ukwa pelela kuti twalolekeshafye pa mulandu wa musebanya no lulumbi, pa mweo na kabili na pamfwa, umulinganya elyo na paluse, ifyo ifyakumanina mulupanda; lelo mu mupwilapo wamaka yama-tontonkanyo yesu tatwinga kwanisha ukumfwikisha ubukankala bwa ciko. Ubutali kabili ubukulu, ukushika kabili nokulepa, uko ukwa kwata ukutemwa uko ukwatulubula kuba ukwa kumfwikafye panono. Ubwanshiko bwepusukilo tabwakomfwike umupwilapo, na panshita iyo abalubulwa bakamona ifyo bakwata ukumonwa kabili nelyo bakeshiba ngefyo baishibikwa; lelo ukupitila fye mumyaka yamuyaya emo icishinka cili no kutwalilila ukusokolwelwa ku mupashi uyo uule papuka no kusansamushiwa.”—The Great Controversy, p. 651.
“Mucicetekelo kuti twakwata ukulolekesha ku nshita iyo iyili no kwisa ku ntanshi no kukwata ukushukila mu bulayo bwakwa Lesa ubwa kulundulula amano yesu, amano ya buntunse ukwampana pamo na yamushilo, namaka yonse aya Mupashi ukuba ayasuntinkana ne ntulo ya lubuto. Tuli no kukwata ukusekela pa mulandu wa kuti fyonse ifya kwata ukutucululusha palwa kusunga kwa-kwa Lesa kuli baifwe fili nokutambalikwa, ifintu ifyo ifyaba ifyakosa ukumfwa fili nokukwata ukulondololwa; na mu fintu fyonse ifyo amalangulushi  yesu aya pelebela yalekwata ukumona icimfulunganya elyo na manshiko ayakwata ukutobaulwa, tuli no kumonamo ukubombela pamo kwa fintu fyonse ukwa wamisha uko ukuli ukwa pwililika. [1 Kolinto 13:12.]”—Steps to Christ, pp. 112, 113.

eng:
5. 	God’s Purpose Toward His People 	Thu, Sep 17
a. 	In what remarkable way has the Lord been unfolding His word in this time as the end approaches? Revelation 10:2, 6, 7.
“The book that was sealed was not the book of Revelation, but that portion of the prophecy of Daniel which related to the last days. . . . (Daniel 12:4) When the book was opened, the proclamation was made, “Time shall be no longer.” (See Revelation 10:6.) The book of Daniel is now unsealed, and the revelation made by Christ to John is to come to all the inhabitants of the earth. By the increase of knowledge a people is to be prepared to stand in the latter days.”—Selected Messages, bk. 2, p. 105.
“Many have entertained the idea that the book of Revelation is a sealed book, and they will not devote time and study to its mysteries. They say that they are to keep looking to the glories of salvation, and that the mysteries revealed to John on the Isle of Patmos are worthy of less consideration than these. But God does not so regard this book. . . .
“The book of Revelation opens to the world what has been, what is, and what is to come; it is for our instruction upon whom the ends of the world are come. It should be studied with reverential awe. . . .
“The Lord Himself revealed to His servant John the mysteries of the book of Revelation, and He designs that they shall be open to the study of all. In this book are depicted scenes that are now in the past, and some of eternal interest that are taking place around us; other of its prophecies will not receive their complete fulfillment until the close of time, when the last great conflict between the powers of darkness and the Prince of heaven will take place.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 7, p. 954.
b. 	What are believers to do in studying Scripture? 2 Timothy 2:15; John 7:17.
bem:
5. UBUFWAYO BWAKWA LESA KUBANTU BAKWE                                  Cisano, Sept 17
a. Nimunshila nshi iya ibelako iya kupapusha intu Imfumu iletwalilila ukosokolwelamo ishiwi lya Iko munshita ino ilyo impela ileya ilepalama? Ubusokololo 10:2, 6, 7.
“Icitabo ico icakakatikwe tecitabo ca Busokololo, lelo nilulya ulubali lwa busesemo bwakwa Daniele ulwa kumine kunshiku shakulekelesha. . . . [Daniele 12:4.] Ilyo icitabo cakwete ukwisulwa, calisoselwe ukuti, “Inshita taili nokutwalilila ukubapo.” (Moneni Ubusokololo 10:6.) Icitabo cakwa Daniele pali nomba calikwata ukufumishiwapo icikakatiko, nobusokololo bwapelwe kuli Yohane ukufuma kuli Klistu buli nokufika kuli bonse abekala pesonde. Ukupitila mu kulundwako kwa bwishibilo abantu bali nokuteyanishiwilwa ku kwimina munshiku shakulekelesha.”—Selected Messages, bk. 2, p. 105.
“Abengi balikwata ukusuminisha ilangulushi ilyakutila icitabo cabusokololo caliba ica kakatikwa, emulandu wine taba bika inshita pambali iyakusambilila bwino ifyankama fyaliko. Batila balingilefye ukulalolesha palulumbi lwaba mwipusukilo, kabili nefyankama fyasokolwelwe kuli Yohane pachishi ca Patmos tafyalingana kuli ifi. Lelo Lesa ena tefyo apenda ibuku ili. . . .
“Ibuku lya Busokololo lilanga kucalo ifyo ifyalipo, ifilipo ilelo, kabili nefili nokubapo; lyaba likambisho lyesu fwebo impela sha chalo shyafikila. Lilingile ukusomwa nomucinshi wabukapepa. . . .
“Imfumu iyine yasokolwele ku mubomfi Waiko Yohane ifyankama ifya mwi buku lya Busokololo , kabili ifyashika no kutila kwingaba ukusambilila ifi ifintu fyonse mukutambalala. Muli ili ibuku mwalilangwa ifikope fya fintu fimo ifyaba ifyakucitika akale, kabili fimbi nafyo fyaba fya pa fintu ifikumine umuyaya ifilechitika pakati kesu; fimbi ifya mabusesemo bwaliko, fimo ifya muli ili ibuku tafili no kufikilishiwa umupwilapo ukufikafye na kubwisaliko bwanshita, ilyo ubulwi ubukalamba ubwakulekelesha pakati ka maka ya mfifi ne Mfumu ya myulu buli no kucitika.”—The SDA Bible Commentary [E. G. White Comments], vol. 7, p. 954.
b. 	Fintu nshi abasumina bafwile ukucita ilyo baLesambilila amalembo ? 2 Timote 2:15; Yohane 7:
